**Moses Aduku Asaga** is a [Ghanaian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghanaian "Ghanaian")[politician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politician "Politician"). He was the [Member of Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Parliament "Member of Parliament") for [Nabdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nabdam_(Ghana_parliament_constituency) "Nabdam (Ghana parliament constituency)") in the [Upper East Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_East_Region "Upper East Region") of [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") from 1997 to 2013. He lost the seat in the December 2012 elections to Boniface Agambilla of the [New Patriotic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Patriotic_Party "New Patriotic Party") (NPP)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-1) who has stood against him in the 2008 election but lost. He was also a [Minister for Employment and Social Welfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Mills_government_ministers "List of Mills government ministers") in Ghana.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-2) He was appointed in early 2012 following a cabinet reshuffle by [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana "President of Ghana")[Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Atta_Mills "John Atta Mills").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-3)

Moses Asaga had been nominated for a ministerial position in 2009 but was withdrawn following a controversy about some ex-gratia awards he had authorised.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-4) After [John Dramani Mahama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mahama "John Mahama") won the 2012 General Elections, he replaced Moses Asaga with Nii Armah Ashietey as Minister of Employment and Social Welfare.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-5) He was then given the position as the C.E.O of the National Petroleum Authority in 2013 by former president John Dramani Mahama

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moses_Asaga&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Moses Asaga holds a [BSc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") in Industrial Chemistry from [Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwame_Nkrumah_University_of_Science_and_Technology "Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology"). He also holds a [MSc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Science "Master of Science") in Petroleum Engineering from [Aberdeen University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aberdeen_University "Aberdeen University") and [MBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Business_Administration "Master of Business Administration"), [Finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finance "Finance") from [Yonsei University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonsei_University "Yonsei University"). In addition to that he has [MPhil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Philosophy "Master of Philosophy") in Financial Economics from [Durham University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durham_University "Durham University"), United Kingdom.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-6)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moses_Asaga&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Asaga is an economist and a banker.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:1-7) He was the manager and project financier of the [Ghana National Petroleum Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation "Ghana National Petroleum Corporation") (GNPC) in Tema.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:2-8)

## Political career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moses_Asaga&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Political career")]

Asaga is a member of the [National Democratic Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Congress_(Ghana) "National Democratic Congress (Ghana)").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:2-8) He became a member of parliament from January 2005 after emerging winner in the General Election in December 2004.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9) He is the MP for [Nabdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nabdam_(Ghana_parliament_constituency) "Nabdam (Ghana parliament constituency)") constituency.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:3-10)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:1-7) He has been elected as the member of parliament for this constituency in fourth and fifth parliament of the fourth Republic of Ghana.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:5-11)

## Elections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moses_Asaga&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Elections")]

Asaga was first elected into Parliament on the ticket of the [National Democratic Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Congress_(Ghana) "National Democratic Congress (Ghana)") with votes representing 8,490 votes out of the 11,348 valid votes cast representing 56.30% over Nicholas Nayembil Nonlant who polled 2,107 votes representing 14.00% and Edward Babah Sampanah who polled 750 votes representing 5.00%.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-12)

He was elected as the member of parliament for the [Nabdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nabdam_(Ghana_parliament_constituency) "Nabdam (Ghana parliament constituency)") constituency of the [Upper East Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_East_Region "Upper East Region") of [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") in the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:0-13)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9) He won on the ticket of the [National Democratic Congress.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Congress_(Ghana) "National Democratic Congress (Ghana)")[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:0-13)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9) His constituency was a part of the 9 parliamentary seats out of 13 seats won by the National Democratic Congress in that election for the Upper East Region.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-14) The [National Democratic Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Congress_(Ghana) "National Democratic Congress (Ghana)") won a minority total of 94 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-15) He was elected with 6,450 votes out of 10,778 total valid votes cast.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:0-13)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9)

This was equivalent to 59.8% of total valid votes cast.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:0-13) He was elected over Somtim Tobiga of the [Peoples’ National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_National_Convention_(Ghana) "People's National Convention (Ghana)"), Boniface Gambila Adagbila of the [New Patriotic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Patriotic_Party "New Patriotic Party") and Tampure Ayenyeta William of the [Convention People's Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convention_People's_Party "Convention People's Party").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:0-13) These obtained 1,002, 3,227 and 99 votes respectively of total votes cast.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:0-13)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9) These were equivalent to 9.3%, 29.9% and 0.9% respectively of total valid votes cast.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:0-13)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9)

In 2008, he won the general elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress for the same constituency.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:2-8) His constituency was part of the 8 parliamentary seats out of 13 seats won by the National Democratic Congress in that election for the Upper East Region.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:6-16) The National Democratic Congress won a minority total of 114 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:6-16)

**Alexander Kofi-Mensah Mould** is a [Ghanaian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghanaian_people "Ghanaian people") politician and banker who is a former [chief executive officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") of [Ghana National Petroleum Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation "Ghana National Petroleum Corporation").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:0-2) He is a member of the [National Democratic Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Congress_(Ghana) "National Democratic Congress (Ghana)").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:1-3) Before he was appointed CEO of GNPC, he was the CEO of National Petroleum Authority.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-4)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alex_Mould&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Alex Mould's parents were W. J. Kwesi Mould of [Jamestown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamestown/Usshertown,_Accra "Jamestown/Usshertown, Accra"), [Accra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra "Accra") and Felicia Awurafua Gsell of [Ejuratia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ejuratia "Ejuratia") in [Kwabre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwabre_East_Municipal_District "Kwabre East Municipal District"), [Ashanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashanti_Region "Ashanti Region").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-5) W. J. Mould was a businessman and a nationalist who was active in Ghana's pre-independence movements, and had attended the [1945 Pan-African Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan-African_Congress "Pan-African Congress") in Manchester as a representative of the Gold Coast Farmers Association.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-6) In 1947, W. J. Mould was the second individual after [George Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Alfred_Grant "George Alfred Grant") to make a financial contribution for the formation of the [United Gold Coast Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Gold_Coast_Convention "United Gold Coast Convention"). Alex's sister, [Betty Mould-Iddrisu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betty_Mould-Iddrisu "Betty Mould-Iddrisu"), has served in government as Minister for Education and also Attorney-General and Minister for Justice.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-7)

Mould attended [Accra Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra_Academy "Accra Academy") from 1973 to 1978 and [Accra High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra_High_School "Accra High School") from 1978 to 1980 for [O-Level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GCE_Ordinary_Level "GCE Ordinary Level") and [A-Level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GCE_Advanced_Level "GCE Advanced Level") qualifications respectively. Mould's father died and was buried in 1980.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-8) He proceeded to the [Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwame_Nkrumah_University_of_Science_and_Technology "Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology"). There, he earned a [bachelor of science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in 1985 in [chemical engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_engineering "Chemical engineering").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:0-2) Mould enrolled at the [College of Petroleum Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_Institute_for_Energy_Studies "Oxford Institute for Energy Studies"), [Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University "Oxford University") where he obtained a [postgraduate diploma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postgraduate_diploma "Postgraduate diploma") in Oil Marketing and Economics in 1989.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:1-3) In 1994, Mould earned a [Master of Business Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Business_Administration "Master of Business Administration") degree in Finance, Accounting and Decision Science from [J. L. Kellogg Graduate School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kellogg_School_of_Management "Kellogg School of Management"), [Northwestern University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwestern_University "Northwestern University"), [Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:0-2)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alex_Mould&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

After graduating from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Mould was posted to undergo a one-year [national service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Service_Secretariat_(Ghana) "National Service Secretariat (Ghana)") at the newly created Ghana National Petroleum Corporation in 1985.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:1-3)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:2-9) After service, he was employed by the corporation as a chemical engineer. He rose through the ranks to become a special assistant to the CEO of GNPC in the area of marketing.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:0-2)

In 1997, Mould resigned from GNPC and was appointed as a senior associate, Structured Trade Finance Americas of [UBS Investment Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UBS_Investment_Bank "UBS Investment Bank") from 1997 to 1999.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:1-3)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:3-10) He moved banks and was employed as associate director of Commodity Finance at [Standard Chartered Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_Chartered_Bank "Standard Chartered Bank") in New York from 1999 to 2001. Mould was moved to the Ghana branch of Standard Chartered Bank in 2001 as executive director and co-head of the wholesale department.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:1-3) He remained in this role until his exit in 2008.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:0-2)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:2-9)

## National appointments

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alex_Mould&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: National appointments")]

When the [John Atta Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Atta_Mills "John Atta Mills") administration was voted into power in 2009, Mould was appointed chief executive officer of the [National Petroleum Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Petroleum_Authority "National Petroleum Authority").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:0-2) He remained in the position till 2012.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:4-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:5-12) In January 2013, when the [John Dramani Mahama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Dramani_Mahama "John Dramani Mahama") administration took over the reins of government, Mould was sent to the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation as its chief executive.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:4-11)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-13)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:3-10) He took over from Nana Boakye Asafu Adjaye, who had headed the corporation since 2009.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:2-9)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:5-12) He remained in the position till the end of the John Mahama administration. In January 2017, he was replaced by [Kofi Koduah Sarpong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong "Kofi Koduah Sarpong").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-:3-10)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alex_Mould&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Mould is a brother to [Betty Mould-Iddrisu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betty_Mould-Iddrisu "Betty Mould-Iddrisu") a former Minister of Justice under the John Atta Mills administration and a former Minister of Education under the John Dramani Mahama administration.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-15) He lost his daughter, Naa Densua to Malaria on 1 January 2020. This was when she was on holiday in [Mauritius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauritius "Mauritius").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould#cite_note-16)

**Kofi Koduah Sarpong** is a [Ghanaian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghanaian_people "Ghanaian people") business executive and consultant. He is a member of the [New Patriotic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Patriotic_Party "New Patriotic Party") of Ghana. He served as Executive Chairman of Ghanaian football club, Kumasi Asante Kotoko from 2010 to 2013.

He has worked for the International Cocoa Organization in London and Ghana Cocoa Board. He is the chief executive officer of [GNPC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation "Ghana National Petroleum Corporation") as of 2017.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-2)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Kofi Sarpong was born at [Nsuta-Beposo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nsuta-Beposo "Nsuta-Beposo") in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:1-4) He obtained his [GCE Ordinary Level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GCE_Ordinary_Level "GCE Ordinary Level") certificate from the [Seventh Day Adventist Secondary School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventh_Day_Adventist_Secondary_School "Seventh Day Adventist Secondary School") in [Bekwai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bekwai "Bekwai") and his [GCE Advanced Level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GCE_Advanced_Level "GCE Advanced Level") from [Sekondi College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sekondi_College "Sekondi College"). He earned a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration from the [University of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Ghana "University of Ghana").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:3-5) He gained a [World Bank scholarship in](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank_scholarship_in?action=edit&redlink=1 "World Bank scholarship in (page does not exist)") 1987 to study a Master of Business Administration from the University of Ghana. Upon completing his master's education, he was awarded a graduate scholarship to pursue a Master of Accountancy at the [University of Glasgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Glasgow "University of Glasgow") in 1990.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:3-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:4-6) A [Commonwealth Scholarship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Scholarship_and_Fellowship_Plan "Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan") offered him the opportunity to apply for a Doctor of Philosophy degree in Industrial and Business Studies from the [University of Warwick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Warwick "University of Warwick") in the United Kingdom.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:5-7) Kofi Sarpong also holds a Master of Arts in Ministry from the [Trinity Theological Seminary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_Theological_Seminary,_Ghana "Trinity Theological Seminary, Ghana"), [Legon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legon "Legon"). He is a [Chartered accountant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chartered_accountant "Chartered accountant") from the [Association of Chartered Certified Accountants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_Chartered_Certified_Accountants "Association of Chartered Certified Accountants"), United Kingdom.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:0-3)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:5-7)

## Working life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Working life")]

Sarpong was employed as an assistant accountant in 1979 at the now defunct Meat Marketing Board.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:1-4) In 1980, he was employed as Deputy Chief Accountant at Ghana Food Distribution Corporation. He was promoted to Chief Accountant and subsequently to general manager of the corporation. He resigned in 1990 to further his studies outside Ghana. Upon his return to Ghana in 1993, Sarpong was employed as Deputy Chief executive of [Ghana Cocoa Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Cocoa_Board "Ghana Cocoa Board").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:4-6) He took up appointment at the [International Cocoa Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Cocoa_Organization "International Cocoa Organization"), London in 1998 and served as the Head of Administration and Financial Services Division in 2001.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:0-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:3-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:4-6)

In 2004, the then [President of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana "President of Ghana"), [John Kufuor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kufuor "John Kufuor"), appointed Sarpong as the Deputy managing director of the [Tema Oil Refinery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tema_Oil_Refinery "Tema Oil Refinery").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:1-4) He was made the managing director of the refinery in 2007. When the John Evans Atta-Mills administration took office in 2009, Sarpong left the position.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:0-3)

From 2010 to 2013, Sarpong served as Executive Chairman of [Kumasi Asante Kotoko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumasi_Asante_Kotoko "Kumasi Asante Kotoko") Sporting Club. He was appointed by [Otumfuo Nana Osei Tutu II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otumfuo_Nana_Osei_Tutu_II "Otumfuo Nana Osei Tutu II"), King of the Asante Kingdom. The club won two [Ghana Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Premier_League "Ghana Premier League") titles, two Champion of Champions titles, and two FA Cup Runners-up positions.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-8) Co-operation agreements with foreign clubs were also established with Sunderland A.F.C. in the United Kingdom, TP Mazembe in DR Congo and Petro Luanda in Angola.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:0-3)

After Asante Kotoko, Sarpong took up the position of Chief executive of The [Global Haulage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Haulage?action=edit&redlink=1 "Global Haulage (page does not exist)") Group, a Ghanaian cocoa buying and exporting company. He was also the chairman of the boards of [The Royal Bank, Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Royal_Bank,_Ghana "The Royal Bank, Ghana") and Imperial General Assurance Ltd.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:0-3)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:4-6)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:3-5) He resigned from boards in 2016.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:3-5)

K.K Sarpong was appointed chancellor of [UPSA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upsala_College "Upsala College") in January 2022.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## CEO of GNPC

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: CEO of GNPC")]

In February 2017, [President Nana Akufo-Addo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nana_Akufo-Addo "Nana Akufo-Addo"), appointed Sarpong as Acting chief executive officer of Ghana National Petroleum Corporation.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:0-3)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:4-6) He replaced [Alex Mould](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mould "Alex Mould") who had served as CEO since 2013.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-:5-7)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Koduah_Sarpong#cite_note-10)

**Moses Aduku Asaga** is a [Ghanaian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghanaian "Ghanaian")[politician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politician "Politician"). He was the [Member of Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Parliament "Member of Parliament") for [Nabdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nabdam_(Ghana_parliament_constituency) "Nabdam (Ghana parliament constituency)") in the [Upper East Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_East_Region "Upper East Region") of [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") from 1997 to 2013. He lost the seat in the December 2012 elections to Boniface Agambilla of the [New Patriotic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Patriotic_Party "New Patriotic Party") (NPP)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-1) who has stood against him in the 2008 election but lost. He was also a [Minister for Employment and Social Welfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Mills_government_ministers "List of Mills government ministers") in Ghana.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-2) He was appointed in early 2012 following a cabinet reshuffle by [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana "President of Ghana")[Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Atta_Mills "John Atta Mills").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-3)

Moses Asaga had been nominated for a ministerial position in 2009 but was withdrawn following a controversy about some ex-gratia awards he had authorised.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-4) After [John Dramani Mahama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mahama "John Mahama") won the 2012 General Elections, he replaced Moses Asaga with Nii Armah Ashietey as Minister of Employment and Social Welfare.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-5) He was then given the position as the C.E.O of the National Petroleum Authority in 2013 by former president John Dramani Mahama

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moses_Asaga&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Moses Asaga holds a [BSc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") in Industrial Chemistry from [Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwame_Nkrumah_University_of_Science_and_Technology "Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology"). He also holds a [MSc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Science "Master of Science") in Petroleum Engineering from [Aberdeen University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aberdeen_University "Aberdeen University") and [MBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Business_Administration "Master of Business Administration"), [Finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finance "Finance") from [Yonsei University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonsei_University "Yonsei University"). In addition to that he has [MPhil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Philosophy "Master of Philosophy") in Financial Economics from [Durham University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durham_University "Durham University"), United Kingdom.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-6)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moses_Asaga&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Asaga is an economist and a banker.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:1-7) He was the manager and project financier of the [Ghana National Petroleum Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation "Ghana National Petroleum Corporation") (GNPC) in Tema.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:2-8)

## Political career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moses_Asaga&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Political career")]

Asaga is a member of the [National Democratic Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Congress_(Ghana) "National Democratic Congress (Ghana)").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:2-8) He became a member of parliament from January 2005 after emerging winner in the General Election in December 2004.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9) He is the MP for [Nabdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nabdam_(Ghana_parliament_constituency) "Nabdam (Ghana parliament constituency)") constituency.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:3-10)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:1-7) He has been elected as the member of parliament for this constituency in fourth and fifth parliament of the fourth Republic of Ghana.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:5-11)

## Elections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moses_Asaga&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Elections")]

Asaga was first elected into Parliament on the ticket of the [National Democratic Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Congress_(Ghana) "National Democratic Congress (Ghana)") with votes representing 8,490 votes out of the 11,348 valid votes cast representing 56.30% over Nicholas Nayembil Nonlant who polled 2,107 votes representing 14.00% and Edward Babah Sampanah who polled 750 votes representing 5.00%.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-12)

He was elected as the member of parliament for the [Nabdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nabdam_(Ghana_parliament_constituency) "Nabdam (Ghana parliament constituency)") constituency of the [Upper East Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_East_Region "Upper East Region") of [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") in the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:0-13)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9) He won on the ticket of the [National Democratic Congress.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Congress_(Ghana) "National Democratic Congress (Ghana)")[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:0-13)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9) His constituency was a part of the 9 parliamentary seats out of 13 seats won by the National Democratic Congress in that election for the Upper East Region.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-14) The [National Democratic Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Congress_(Ghana) "National Democratic Congress (Ghana)") won a minority total of 94 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-15) He was elected with 6,450 votes out of 10,778 total valid votes cast.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:0-13)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9)

This was equivalent to 59.8% of total valid votes cast.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:0-13) He was elected over Somtim Tobiga of the [Peoples’ National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_National_Convention_(Ghana) "People's National Convention (Ghana)"), Boniface Gambila Adagbila of the [New Patriotic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Patriotic_Party "New Patriotic Party") and Tampure Ayenyeta William of the [Convention People's Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convention_People's_Party "Convention People's Party").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:0-13) These obtained 1,002, 3,227 and 99 votes respectively of total votes cast.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:0-13)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9) These were equivalent to 9.3%, 29.9% and 0.9% respectively of total valid votes cast.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:0-13)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:4-9)

In 2008, he won the general elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress for the same constituency.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:2-8) His constituency was part of the 8 parliamentary seats out of 13 seats won by the National Democratic Congress in that election for the Upper East Region.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:6-16) The National Democratic Congress won a minority total of 114 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:6-16)

He was elected with 5,369 votes out of 11,230 total valid votes cast.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:7-17)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:5-11) This was equivalent to 47.81% of total valid votes cast.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:5-11)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:7-17) He was elected over Boniface Agambila Adagbila of the [New Patriotic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Patriotic_Party "New Patriotic Party"), Somtim Tobiga of the [People's National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_National_Convention_(Ghana) "People's National Convention (Ghana)") and Tampugre Ayenyeta William of the [Convention People's Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convention_People's_Party "Convention People's Party").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:5-11)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:7-17) These obtained 45.39%, 6.37% and 0.44% respectively of the total votes cast.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:5-11)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Asaga#cite_note-:7-17)

The **Ghana National Petroleum Corporation** (**GNPC**) is a state agency responsible for the exploration, licensing, and distribution of petroleum-related activities in [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation#cite_note-ABOUT-2)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

GNPC is Ghana's National Oil Company (NOC) which was established in 1983 to replace the Petroleum Department which was an agency under the Ministry of Fuel and power.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation#cite_note-6) The department was responsible for the importation of crude oil and [petroleum products](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petroleum_products "Petroleum products") for the Ghanaian economy.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation#cite_note-ABOUT-2) The mandate for oil exploration was held to be the Technical Directorate of the Ministry of Fuel and Power and the Geological Survey Department. The corporation was created to promote the Government of Ghana's objective of supplying adequate and reliable petroleum for the country and the discovery of crude oil in the country's territories. And also to help in reducing the country's dependence on crude oil imports, through the development of the country's own petroleum resources.[](https://www.devex.com/organizations/ghana-national-petroleum-corporation-gnpc-143202)

In 2025, GNPC signed an energy cooperation pact with Eni and partners of the Offshore Cape Three Points (OCTP) aimed at increasing oil and gas production while also promoting sustainable initiatives. [[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation#cite_note-7)

## Mandate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Mandate")]

The corporation was established as a state-owned company with the statutory backing of [PNDC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PNDC "PNDC") Laws 64 and 84. The laws mandated the corporation to engage in exploration, production and disposal of petroleum products. The laws also established the legal structure that informed the corporation in contractual agreements between the Government of Ghana and private [oil exploration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_exploration "Oil exploration") companies. In 1987, the Petroleum [Income Tax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Income_Tax "Income Tax") Law were added to the corporation's mandate to permit it to tax various petroleum products for consumption. The law was the PNDC Law 188.

## Functions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Functions")]

Promoting petroleum exploration efforts is one of the corporation's duties. The institution also appraises existing petroleum discoveries, and to ensure that [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") benefits the most from the development of the country's petroleum resources. The corporation promotes the training of [Ghanaians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghanaians "Ghanaians") in petroleum-related activities and ensures [environmental protection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_protection "Environmental protection") in all petroleum-related activities.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation#cite_note-10)

## Jubilee fields

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Jubilee fields")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Jubilee_Oil_Field_of_the_Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation_%28GNPC%29_and_National_Petroleum_Authority.png/250px-Jubilee_Oil_Field_of_the_Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation_%28GNPC%29_and_National_Petroleum_Authority.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jubilee_Oil_Field_of_the_Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation_(GNPC)_and_National_Petroleum_Authority.png)

[Jubilee Oil Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jubilee_oil_field "Jubilee oil field") of the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) and [National Petroleum Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Petroleum_Authority "National Petroleum Authority") located off the coast of the [Western Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Region_(Ghana) "Western Region (Ghana)") in [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") in the [South Atlantic Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Atlantic_Ocean "South Atlantic Ocean").

The corporation announced in 2007 that the Petroleum Agreement signed in 2004 had yielded in the discovery of oil in commercial quantities.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation#cite_note-CONTR-11) Production of crude oil begun in December 2010. The country's oil fields are known as [Jubilee fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jubilee_oil_field "Jubilee oil field") and is situated at Cape Three Points in the [Western region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Region_(Ghana) "Western Region (Ghana)") of the country. The corporation has controlling stake in all the oil wells that produce crude oil. In April 2011, GNPC [Archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20231003211912/https://www.gnpcghana.com/overview.html) 3 October 2023 at the [Wayback Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayback_Machine "Wayback Machine") confirmed that it had an initial 10% interest in a new oil discovery at the Paradise prospect offshore Ghana. The discovery was announced in April 2011 by [Hess Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hess_Corporation "Hess Corporation"), a [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)") based oil company.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation#cite_note-HESS-12) In June 2011, the corporation lifted 135,675 metric tonnes of Jubilee crude oil from the [FPSO Kwame Nkrumah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FPSO_Kwame_Nkrumah "FPSO Kwame Nkrumah"). This represented crude oil on behalf of the Ghana Group, comprising the [Government of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Ghana "Government of Ghana") (GoG) and GNPC. It represented the first lifting of crude oil from the Jubilee fields. The barrels lifted comprised accumulated government royalties of 37,557 metric tonnes and accumulated GNPC's 13.75 per cent participating interest entitlement of 98,119 metric tonnes.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_National_Petroleum_Corporation#cite_note-FPSO-13)

⚽ Women’s Football & The Diaspora: Zimbabwe’s Untapped Frontier For too long, the conversation around "Bridging Worlds" in football has centred on the men’s game. But half of our football ecosystem remains a vastly underutilised resource: women’s football. As Zimbabwe reimagines its football future, integrating the diaspora must include the women’s game not as an afterthought, but as a central pillar of national progress. Across the globe, Zimbabwean women are excelling as players, coaches, managers, and mentors in professional environments. Yet, they lack a direct pathway to contribute their expertise back home. We can learn from pioneers like Nigeria, South Africa, and Morocco, whose success stems from intentional diaspora inclusion and investment. Here are three pathways to integration for Zimbabwe: 1️⃣ Diaspora Talent Identification: Create a digital registry to profile players, coaches, and sports scientists abroad, turning it into a live scouting and mentorship hub for local academies. 2️⃣ Coaching & Mentorship Networks: Link diaspora professionals with grassroots programs through annual summits and online exchanges to cultivate leadership and professionalism in the next generation. 3️⃣ Investment in Visibility & Infrastructure: Foster collaborations between diaspora investors, local clubs, and media to transform coverage and facilities. Imagine local women’s leagues being livestreamed to inspire girls in Harare and Leeds alike. The goal is a shift in narrative—from one of resilience to one of opportunity. It’s about crafting a story where Zimbabwean women are leading in innovation, coaching, and administration. The future of our football depends on a united global community. The talent is ready. The game is ready. Now, the system must be ready too. Day 1: The Divide – From Suspicion to Synergy in Zimbabwean Football To bridge the gap between Zimbabwe’s diaspora talent and our local football structures, we must first understand its origins. The journey from suspicion to synergy requires a crucial mindset shift. The chasm wasn't created overnight. It was carved by isolated incidents, systemic inertia, and a fundamental clash of perspectives. The Two Sides of the Divide: · The Local Viewpoint: Diaspora players are sometimes viewed with suspicion—seen as privileged, "difficult to manage," or lacking the commitment of those developed in the local system. Past scandals have framed their engagement as a transactional risk. · The Diaspora Viewpoint: Engaging with Zimbabwean football can feel like navigating a labyrinth. The lack of professional structures, consistent communication, and long-term planning is frustrating for those accustomed to organized environments. The central question is one of trust. This mutual misunderstanding is our greatest barrier, perpetuating a false division between "local" and "import." The Mindset Shift: From Gatekeeping to Stewardship The transformation we need is foundational. We must move: · From Threat to Tide: Diaspora talent isn't taking a spot from a local player; it's raising the level of competition, introducing new techniques, and expanding the footballing IQ of the entire squad. · From Transaction to Investment: It’s not just about capping a player for one tournament. It’s about a long-term investment in our national football ecosystem by integrating their knowledge, discipline, and networks. · From Ad-Hoc to Proactive: We must move beyond last-minute calls and build a transparent, welcoming pathway for any Zimbabwean, anywhere, to contribute. The divide was built on outdated notions. Our future depends on our ability to dismantle them and embrace a new, inclusive philosophy. Our strength has always been our people; it's time we started acting like it. What is the most critical mindset shift needed to bridge such divides in sports or other industries? **MultiChoice** is a [South African](link_12) company, owned by [French](link_30) media conglomerate [Canal+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal+_S.A [link_28]. "Canal+ S.A."), that operates [DStv](link_20), a major [satellite television](link_19) service in [Sub-Saharan Africa](link_13). It also operates [GOtv](link_21), a minor terrestrial TV service operating in 9 countries, and formerly [Showmax](link_31), a [subscription video on-demand](link_32)[over-the-top](link_33)[streaming](link_34) service.

## Overview

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=MultiChoice&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Overview")]

MultiChoice was formed out of the subscriber-management branch of the [M-Net](link_4)[terrestrial](link_35)[pay television](link_9) company, and broadcasts the full range of M-Net channels on the DStv service. MultiChoice is owned by the media conglomerate of the same name.

One of the subsidiaries of MultiChoice is **DStv Stream**, formally DStv Now then DStv App, a service that delivers television transmission to mobile devices such as laptops, smart phones and notebooks.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MultiChoice#cite_note-PRNEWS-3)

Formerly under [NetHold](link_36), it had operations in the Scandinavian, Benelux, Central Europe, Greek & Cypriot regions under the [Filmnet](link_37) TV service, [Italy](link_38) via [Telepiù](link_39), [Egypt](link_40) under [CNE (Cable Network of Egypt)](link_41), Middle East under Gulf TV and [Arab Radio and Television Network](link_42)& Thailand under [UBC (United Broadcasting Corporation)](link_43).

In 2020, MultiChoice had a total subscriber base of 20.1 million viewers throughout Africa, and [Naspers](link_44) asserted that MultiChoice was one of the fastest growing pay-TV operators globally.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MultiChoice#cite_note-MyBroad-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MultiChoice#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MultiChoice#cite_note-6)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=MultiChoice&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

### Early years (1983–1991)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=MultiChoice&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early years (1983–1991)")]

In 1983, [Koos Bekker](link_45) wrote a paper at [Columbia University](link_46) describing the idea that led to [M-Net](link_4), and along with two others pitched the idea to [Naspers](link_44), which acquired a 26% share, leading to Naspers executive Ton Vosloo serving as chair of the board.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MultiChoice#cite_note-7) M-Net lost money in its first few years.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MultiChoice#cite_note-8)

### Expansion (1992–2017)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=MultiChoice&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Expansion (1992–2017)")]

In 1993, M-Net was divided into two divisions, one focused on transmission of the entertainment channels and the other on cellphone operations, signal distribution and subscriber management. This second division became MultiChoice. The company had been granted a licence to broadcast into Namibia in 1991 and, as a result, in 1996 MultiChoice Africa was established.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MultiChoice#cite_note-ITWEB-9)

In 1992, analogue services were launched in 20 African countries and lasted until 1996 when digital services replaced them. This division, called [DStv (Digital Satellite Television)](link_20), had first been launched in South Africa on October 6, 1995, making it the first direct-to-home digital pay-TV service outside the US.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MultiChoice#cite_note-ITWEB-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Television service provider in Barbados

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/ae/Mctv_barbados.jpg/250px-Mctv_barbados.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mctv_barbados.jpg)

Multi-Choice TV

**Multi-Choice TV** (**MCTV**) is a [television](link_2) service provider in [Barbados](link_3).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-Choice_TV#cite_note-1) It is a [Multichannel Multipoint Distribution Service](link_4) (MMDS) or [DVB-C](link_5)[Wireless](link_6)[microwave](link_7)-based broadcast subscription television provider. They offer a variety of packages which can be considered as comparatively priced to similar providers throughout the world.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Multi-Choice_TV&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The service began operating on December 14, 1987, under the name Subscription Television (STV), which had very few channels offered. The main channels were [CNN](link_8), [ESPN](link_9), and [Lifetime Television](link_10), with an occasional option of [pay per view](link_11) (PPV) being offered for local special events and the occasional international PPV sports broadcast. In 1996 it was upgraded to include a new platform called Multi-Choice TV which was an [analog](link_12) wireless microwave broadcast offering many more channels (e.g. the [BBC](link_13), Canada's [CBC](link_14) and [TBN](link_15)), eventually reaching [bandwidth](link_16) capacity and having to upgrade the service to a [digital](link_17) broadcast system. Multi-Choice TV have not fully converted all of its subscribers yet. The system relies on [line-of-sight propagation](link_18) so total island wide coverage has proved to be a problem and the provider is looking into alternatives. A recent press release has indicated their interest in a partnership with the local [telco](link_19)[LIME](link_20).

The service uses a [Yagi antenna](link_21) to receive the encrypted broadcast, which in turn is then decrypted by the provider's set top box. The provider has faced the challenge of signal theft by pirates using modified DVB-C compatible receivers and PCI cards. Some of the most popular being the "Dreambox" manufactured in [Germany](link_22) to decode their signal which is based on [Nagravision](link_23) which is a conditional access control system developed by the [Kudelski Group](link_24). In order to prevent such activity in August, 2006 the [Government of Barbados](link_25) stiffened the local Barbadian copyright laws, in addition to a strengthening of the laws on cable TV piracy. The CBC provider is planning for further circumvention of the Dream boxes in 2009.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-Choice_TV#cite_note-2)

In 2014, MCTV announced that it would begin carrying new channels such as MovieCity Action (now Star Action), MovieCity Hollywood (now Star Hits), [AMC](link_26), [KTLA](link_27), [WGN](link_28), Disney, and the [NBC Sports Network](link_30). They also introduced 20 HD channels, such as [ABC](link_31), [NBC](link_29), [CBS](link_32)&[FOX](link_33) and also released new PVR boxes. MCTV also introduced a new slogan, _MCTV the Right Choice_.

Multi-Choice TV also competes against the [US](link_34)-based [direct broadcast satellite](link_35) (DBS) service provider [DirecTV](link_36) in Barbados. The service uses the [NTSC](link_37) television format.

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Multi-Choice_TV&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: References")]

1.   [↑](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-Choice_TV#cite_ref-1 "Jump up")[Barbados: Society](link_43), Commonwealth of Nations
2.   [↑](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-Choice_TV#cite_ref-2 "Jump up")Alleyne, Barry (28 November 2009). ["DREAM OVER"](link_44). _[Nation Newspaper](link_46)_. Archived from [the original](link_45) on 2009-12-03. Retrieved 2 December 2009. Our investigations also discovered that Dream Box users were able to get a free service since early 2008, because CBC's old encryption software only scrambled their MCTV signal every two minutes, which allowed the Dream Box to recover the signal. But the new security will leave the Dream Boxes crippled. "This is a money business, and encryption is always changing, and not cheap. The new software will actually scramble the MCTV signal every ten to 15 seconds, so Dream Boxes will not be able to keep up, and eventually lose the entire signal," the source added.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

South African businessman (born 1952)

| Koos Bekker |
| --- |
| Born | (1952-12-14) 14 December 1952 (age 73) [Potchefstroom](link_3), [North West](link_4), South Africa |
| Education | [University of the Witwatersrand](link_5) [Columbia University](link_6) |
| Occupation | Chair of [Naspers](link_7) |
| Spouse | Karen Roos |
| Children | 4 |

**Jacobus Petrus** "**Koos**" **Bekker** (born 14 December 1952) is a South African [billionaire](link_8)[businessman](link_9), and the chairman of [Prosus](link_10), and [Naspers](link_7), a global consumer internet group and one of the largest technology investors and operators in the world.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-Naspers-1) The company operates in 130 countries and is listed on the [London Stock Exchange](link_11) and [Johannesburg Stock Exchange](link_12). It has the largest [market capitalization](link_13) of any media company outside the United States and China. As of January 2025, his net worth was estimated at US$2.9 billion.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-Forbes_profile-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koos_Bekker&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Koos Bekker was born in [Potchefstroom](link_3), South Africa in 1952.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-Rum01-3):17 He attended Hoër Volkskool Heidelberg and completed degrees at [Stellenbosch University](link_14), in law and literature, and at [Wits University](link_15), in law.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] He holds an MBA from [Columbia Business School](link_16),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-Rum01-3):17 New York and an honorary doctorate from [Stellenbosch University](link_14).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koos_Bekker&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

After a few years in advertising, he received an MBA degree from [Columbia Business School](link_16), graduating in 1984. As a result of a project paper, he, with a few young colleagues, founded one of the first two pay-television services outside of the United States. [M-Net](link_17) and its sister companies, such as Multichoice, eventually expanded to 48 countries across Africa. In the 1990s, he was a founding director of mobile communication company [MTN](link_18).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-4) In 1997 Bekker became CEO of Naspers, one of the initial investors in the M-Net/Multichoice group.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Naspers bought out the other shareholders. During his tenure, the market capitalization of Naspers grew from about $1.2 billion to $45 billion. His compensation package was unusual in that for fifteen years as CEO he earned no salary, bonus or perks. He was compensated solely via stock option grants that vested over time.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Under Bekker, Naspers invested in pay television, mobile telephony and various internet services, which included buying part of the Chinese Internet firm [Tencent](link_19) as an anchor shareholder from 2001, with a current stake of 23%.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-Forbes_profile-2)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-5) Over time, the Naspers Prosus group expanded into various sectors of the consumer internet including classified services, food delivery and payment systems.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-6) The group conducts business in Europe, Africa, Latin America, India and South Africa with a group market capitalization of US$124 billion.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-7)

In 2020, former South African Minister for Communications, [Yunus Carrim](link_20) testified to the [Zondo Commission](link_21) into State Capture that Bekker had played a significant role in irregularly pressuring government officials to protect MultiChoice's effective monopoly over South Africa's pay-TV sector. The Zondo Commission found no wrongdoing on the part of MultiChoice.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-8)

The Constitutional Court has held that Government's digital migration policy is not centered around individual players in the broadcasting industry and that the policy decision to dump decryption capability in government subsidized DTT set top boxes was in the best interests of the poor and the broader public. _[Electronic Media Network Limited and Others v e.tv (Pty) Limited and Others_ 2017 (9) BCLR 1108 (CC).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-9)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Koos_Bekker&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Bekker is married to Karen Roos, has two children and resides in Cape Town, South Africa.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-Forbes_profile-2) The couple have been responsible for developing [Hadspen House](link_22) near [Castle Cary](link_23) in [Somerset](link_24), England, as The Newt in Somerset, a luxury hotel and visitor attraction in extensive grounds.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-10) Since 2022, The Newt has been the primary sponsor of the [Chelsea Flower Show](link_25).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-11)

Bekker has also owned [Babylonstoren](link_26), a wine estate in the [Drakenstein Valley](link_27) in the [Cape Winelands](link_28), [South Africa](link_29), since 2007. [[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-12) As one of the oldest [Cape Dutch](link_30) houses in South Africa, the estate is a popular tourist attraction and hotel with its garden inspired by the historic [Company's Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Company [link_31]'s_Garden "Company's Garden") in Cape Town. [[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koos_Bekker#cite_note-13)

**Digital Satellite Television**, abbreviated **DStv**, is a [South African](link_12)[direct broadcast satellite](link_13) company owned by [MultiChoice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MultiChoice "MultiChoice"). The company provides [audio](link_14), [radio](link_15), and [television channels](link_16) and related services to subscribers across [Africa](link_6). Most subscribers reside in South Africa, Nigeria, and Zimbabwe.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-2)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-3)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-4)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DStv&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

In 1986, pay-television came to South Africa when a single-channel analogue service, [M-Net](link_17), was launched by [Naspers](link_18) and local businesses/companies. For almost seven years, all of M-Net's operations were handled by a single dedicated company until 1995 when a second subsidiary company, [MultiChoice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MultiChoice "MultiChoice"), was launched.

MultiChoice would take over the operations of M-Net including decoder sales, subscriber services, which were also available in local stores, and account management. MultiChoice would also embark on establishing presence in multiple countries outside South Africa.

Not long after, a digital satellite service in [South Africa](link_12) was announced by [MultiChoice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MultiChoice "MultiChoice") and was launched that same year on 6 October 1995 as _DStv_, an abbreviation for _Digital Satellite Television_. On its launch, DStv offered a package of 16 channels: [Cartoon Network](link_19), [CNN](link_20), a 40-channel [DMX](link_21) audio service, [ESPN](link_22), [Hallmark](link_23), [K-T.V.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-T.V [link_24]. "K-T.V."), [M-Net](link_17), [Movie Magic](link_25), [SelecTV](link_26), [Sky News](link_27), [SuperSport](link_28), [TNT](link_29), [Travel Channel](link_30), the [Trinity Broadcasting Network](link_31), [TV5 Afrique](link_32), [MTV](link_33) and [VH1](link_34).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-Africa_turns_on-5) The launch of DStv was deemed "satisfactory", with decoder sales having surpassed 10,000 units by November 1995.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-6)

This prompted changes to the main M-Net channel, which, while having its formula unchanged, started concentrating more on African productions, while K-T.V., Movie Magic and SuperSport gained their own separate channels. Aside from the DMX service, subscribers also had access to Radio 702 and [Voice of America](link_35). Multichoice expected the number of channels to be increased to 24 by early 1996.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-Africa_turns_on-5)

Within weeks of its launch, DStv added its first new channels, [Discovery Channel](link_36) and [BBC World](link_37). The latter was available over the terrestrial frequencies of M-Net eleven hours a day; this enabled subscribers to watch the channel 24/7.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-7) By September 1996, DStv had 55,000 subscribers.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-8)

In February 1998, DStv had 70,000 subscribers across the continent. By June that year, the number skyrocketed to 215,000 in Sub-Saharan Africa and 31,000 in Egypt and the Middle East. With the launch of [BBC Prime](link_38) in March 1999, it had risen to nearly 350,000, an increase of 30% within the past ten months. This also coincided with the arrival of National Geographic Channel and the South African business network Summit.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-9)

Interactive services started in 2000 with six datacasting channels aimed primarily at the South African market. These channels featured games, news, weather, and soon, the possibility of accessing internet services, banking, video-on-demand and camera angles during key sporting events.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-10)

Over the 2 decades since then till today, television channels launch on the platform when channel carriage contracts are signed and/or renewed between MultiChoice and another [media conglomerate](link_39)/[broadcaster](link_40) and ceases transmission when channel carriage contracts are not renewed or by decisions made by the latter.

In July 2003, DSTV launched [Africa Magic](link_41) as a movie and general entertainment channel geared at showcasing Nollywood talent and African culture. At the time of its launch it received high popularity amongst DStv subscribers, especially in South Africa and Nigeria.

This was followed by the launch of new services including: W4 Eutelsat satellite with Ku-band services to [Sub-Saharan Africa](link_42) and the [Indian Ocean Islands](link_43) in 2000 (which Multichoice bought five transponders),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-11)[Interactive Television](link_44) in 2002, the Dual-view decoder in 2003, and the DStv PVR decoder and the DStv Compact subscription package bundle in 2005.

Thanks to the new contract with Eutelsat, DStv vastly improved its channel offer by starting Ku-band signals in West Africa, as well as the inclusion of new Lusophone channels in Angola and Mozambique ([RTP Internacional](link_45) – already in South Africa up until then, [SIC Internacional](link_46) and [TV Globo Internacional](link_47)), three channels from India (Sony Entertainment Television India, B4U and Zee TV) and the possibility of adding Arab and Lebanese channels in West Africa.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-12)

The interactive services were provided by American company OpenTV and launched in the first half of 2002.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-13) SuperSport had already started an interactive service, SuperSport Zone, in May 2001.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-14) By March 2002, the roll-out was completed, by means of a new decoder, 720i.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-15)

In November 2006, DSTV added KBC and KTN to its Kenyan subscribers' package.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DStv#cite_note-16)

Title: Muse — Your Personal AI Agent

URL Source: https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://muse.ai/&h=AUAFTeX0MyELaOVJHPD9k4PsVcBroBmnHvd4NC1R9B6cJ0rzhOKvZ60Fns_ErzS3JfSvYzI8ZoKehE-wO3PgQjx66hSnMgyr2lFUDPARQ_gI0CaxMZiESCWPV3mOIAzFkV0zbuMHyYQWoQ

Markdown Content:
Log in

![Image 1: Muse](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/brand/muse-logo.svg)
# Muse, AI that gets it done for you Muse[Video 1](https://l.facebook.com/videos/avatars/hatch_connecting.mp4)[Video 2](https://l.facebook.com/videos/avatars/hatch_working.mp4), AI that gets it done for you sorts your email books reservations shops for you saves you money manages calendars builds fitness plans gets it done for you sorts your email![Image 2](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-envelope.webp)books reservations![Image 3](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-airplane.webp)shops for you![Image 4](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-cart.webp)saves you money![Image 5](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-piggybank.webp)manages calendars![Image 6](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-calendar.webp)builds fitness plans![Image 7](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/b-01.webp)gets it done for you

# Log in or create an account

Mobile number or email(required) 

You may receive SMS notifications from us by using your mobile number. [Learn more](https://www.meta.com/help/artificial-intelligence/31983416211257755/)

Continue

[Learn more](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://muse.ai/&h=AUAFTeX0MyELaOVJHPD9k4PsVcBroBmnHvd4NC1R9B6cJ0rzhOKvZ60Fns_ErzS3JfSvYzI8ZoKehE-wO3PgQjx66hSnMgyr2lFUDPARQ_gI0CaxMZiESCWPV3mOIAzFkV0zbuMHyYQWoQ#landing-introduction-video-title)

## Built around your whole life

Give Muse a goal or task and it handles the rest, from saving money and improving your health to smart shopping and helping you strengthen your relationships.

[Video 3](https://scontent.xx.fbcdn.net/o1/v/t6/f2/m421/AQPvdntV2G814fVexG62mHy9MLAFz-IUx2_276pwlTOScjlG7403bT1NxrxgW2yToPZR5BOsHoRWgC3EQGGX.mp4?_nc_sid=9c7e41&_nc_ht=scontent.xx.fbcdn.net&ccb=17-1&_nc_gid=ydbDT7iYg1MX2NBLqRZyBQ&edm=AIlawRcEAAAA&_nc_zt=28&oh=00_AQOyzscFO6qFwmd--uljvrO__od_XrEA9sLxsqC0X_G7dg&oe=6AEB38AE#t=1)

### Every Muse user shares their own computer in the cloud with their Muse.

Muse Secure VM is a persistent, isolated Linux computer with a full browser that you and your agent can use to complete tasks, allowing you to intervene at any point. It's your computer and your browser, with the storage, CPU, and memory to handle real work.

![Image 8: Floating browser, search, map, calendar, and confirmation panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/browser.webp)![Image 9: Floating browser, search, map, calendar, and confirmation panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/browser-dark.webp)

### Designed around the way you already communicate

Chat with your agent in the same way you message with other people, using the Muse app on mobile, Mac, or directly in WhatsApp. There's no learning curve, just tell Muse what you want to get done.

![Image 10: A chat on a phone where the agent has filled out a school form, shown beside a laptop](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/messaging.webp)![Image 11: A chat on a phone where the agent has filled out a school form, shown beside a laptop](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/messaging-dark.webp)

### Stay in control of what your agent does

Approve actions your agent takes on your behalf before they happen, like sending emails and making purchases. See a complete audit trail of everything your agent has done (and what it's planning to do).

![Image 12: Floating purchase, message, activity, permission, and decision controls](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/approvals.webp)![Image 13: Floating purchase, message, activity, permission, and decision controls](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/approvals-dark.webp)

### Your data is kept secure and private

Save your logins to a secure credential store Muse can't see, with 1Password integration coming soon. When shopping, a one-time card number is generated at checkout so your real card stays hidden from the merchant and your agent. Eligible purchases are covered by [Link's purchase protections](https://link.com/protections), a first for AI agents, and your conversations are not shared with Meta's ad systems.

![Image 14: A vault, privacy shield, masked credential, security control, and virtual card](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/secure-storage.webp)![Image 15: A vault, privacy shield, masked credential, security control, and virtual card](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/secure-storage-dark.webp)

### Proactively helps with your goals and suggests ideas

Muse helps you stay on top of things, takes tasks and projects off your plate, and turns long-term goals into real progress. It learns from conversations, reflects on what matters and gets sharper, coming back with ideas built around what you actually need, ready to act on them under your direction.

![Image 16: Floating checklist, calendar, route, progress, and idea panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/goals.webp)![Image 17: Floating checklist, calendar, route, progress, and idea panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/goals-dark.webp)

### Connects to your apps and builds its own tools

Connect the apps you use daily, like email, calendar, and Instagram. You decide what your agent can see and what it can do. If a task needs a tool that doesn't exist, your agent builds it for you.

![Image 18: Connected app, messaging, media, cloud, calendar, and automation tiles](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/connectors.webp)

## Get the most out of your Muse

A guided tour of Muse, from setting a first goal to seeing it through.

![Image 19: Product designer presenting a guided tour of Muse](https://l.facebook.com/images/hatch/landing/product-walkthrough-cover.png)

## Learn more about Muse

Explore the choices behind Muse and how it is built to deserve your trust.

### [How We Designed Muse When Muse works, it feels like magic. These are the product choices that make the experience possible.](https://introducing.muse.ai/)### [How We Built Safety Into Muse Muse is built for privacy, safety, and security. Learn how these principles shape every part of the product.](https://security.muse.ai/)### [Muse for Business Meet the AI agent that works for your small business and keeps jobs moving between your decisions.](https://l.facebook.com/business)

## Ready to try Muse?

# Create a LinkedIn Page

 Last updated: 1 year ago 

### Create a LinkedIn Page

Connect with clients, employees, and the LinkedIn community.

[Create](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/feature-launcher/urn:li:helpCenterArticle:(543852,LITHOGRAPH)?trk=search_feature_launcher)

You can create a LinkedIn Page for free, helping you represent and build your organization’s brand on LinkedIn. Pages can help LinkedIn members learn about your business, brand, products and services, and job opportunities.

You must have a LinkedIn account to create a Page. Before you create one, we recommend reviewing our best practices.

### Important to know

You can create a LinkedIn Page either using the desktop version or using the LinkedIn mobile app on an iOS device. Creating a LinkedIn Page is not supported on Android mobile devices.

Desktop iOS

To create a Page:

1.   Click the **For Business** icon in the upper-right corner of your LinkedIn homepage. 
2.   Scroll down and click **Create a Company Page** . 
3.   
Select the Page type:

    *   Company
    *   Showcase page
    *   Educational institution

4.   Enter your **Page identity, Company or Institution details**, and **Profile details** information. 
5.   Select the verification box to confirm that you have the right to act on behalf of the company or school. 
6.   Click the **Create page** button. 

    *   If you receive an error message, try our troubleshooting tips for creating your Page.

7.   Click **Start building your page!** to complete your LinkedIn Page. 

To create a Page:

1.   Go to any LinkedIn Page. 
2.   Tap the **More** icon on the right and select **Create a LinkedIn Page**. 
3.   Select the Page type: 

    *   Company
    *   Educational institution

4.   Enter your **Company name**, **LinkedIn public URL**, **Website**, **Industry**, **Company size**, **Company type**, and **Tagline** (optional). 
5.   Tap the verification box to confirm that you have the right to act on behalf of the company or school. 
6.   Tap **Create** in the upper-right corner. 

### Here's a tip

As an admin, you can also convert your Page. Learn more about the different types of [LinkedIn Pages](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a727893).

**Results**

Once you’ve created a Page, you become the super admin of the Page and can assign others to be admins of your Page.

## WE EXPECTED SOME QUESTIONS

![Image 45](https://dstv.com/media/wvdahp53/card-deck-faq.png?mode=crop&width=600)

What's changing?

From 17 September, DStv is introducing its biggest package update in 15 years, with more choice, more content and more value.

Some of our biggest channels, including M-Net,kykNET and Mzansi Magic, will now be available on more accessible packages than before.Sport is opening up too, with full PSL coverage available on Select and our first sports-focused package, Sports, bringing together 17 dedicated sports channels, including every PSL, Premier League and UEFA Champions League match, plus cricket.Access becomes Starter, Family becomes Select, and Compact becomes Sports, with more channels and content added to each.There’s also a brand-new Movies & Series package created for entertainment lovers.

Will I pay more?

No. Prices stay the same; you're just getting more content.

Will I lose any channels?

No. In fact, the new line-up gives customers more to watch.

Starter gains 10 channels, Select gains 10 channels and Sports gains four channels.Movies & Series is an entirely new package for entertainment lovers, while Premium continues to bring together DStv’s most comprehensive entertainment and sport offering, including exclusive premium sport.

A few existing channels are also coming together to create bigger, stronger destinations. For example, Mzansi Wethu, Mzansi Bioskop and Mzansi Music come together in Wethu+, giving viewers a broader mix of great local entertainment in one place.

What if I'm on Compact Plus? 

You stay on Compact Plus, with no change to your account. The package will no longer be available to new customers, but existing Compact Plus customers can continue enjoying it as usual.

Do I need to do anything today?

No.There’s nothing you need to do right now. If you’re an active DStv customer, your package will update automatically when the new line-up launches on 17 September.

If I want to change my package, what do I need to do?

From 17 September,you’ll be able to upgrade, sign up or change your package through our self-service channels.

With more choice across entertainment, sport and movies and series, you can pick the DStv package that best fits what you love to watch.

What if I'm on Premium or EasyView?

You stay on the package you have.There’s no change to Premium or EasyView.

Premium remains DStv’s most comprehensive package, with the widest combination of entertainment and sport, including our exclusive premium sport.

When are the new packages available?

The new DStv packages launch in South Africa on 17 September 2026.That’s when you can start enjoying more choice and more to watch.

 Do I need to reconnect or do anything to switch? 

If you’re an active customer,there’s nothing you need to do.We’ll take care of the switch automatically.

When will I hear more?

We’ll contact you directly by email or SMS with the details of what the changes mean for your package, so you’ll know exactly what to expect.

Where can I find more information?

Head to [dstv.com](https://dstv.com/en-za/news/149042/complete-guide-to-new-dstv-packages "New DStv packages: What to expect") for the full breakdown of the new packages.
