The **president of the Republic of Ghana** is the elected [head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state") and [head of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government") of [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana"), as well as [commander-in-chief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander-in-chief "Commander-in-chief") of the [Ghana Armed Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Armed_Forces "Ghana Armed Forces"). The current president of Ghana is [John Mahama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Dramani_Mahama "John Dramani Mahama"), who won the [2024 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Ghanaian_general_election "2024 Ghanaian general election") against then vice president, [Mahamudu Bawumia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia "Mahamudu Bawumia"), by a margin of 14.94%. He was sworn into office on 7 January 2025.

## History of the office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=President_of_Ghana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History of the office")]

From 1957 to 1960 the head of state under the [Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Ghana "Constitution of Ghana") of 1957 was the [queen of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_of_Ghana "Queen of Ghana"), [Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_II "Elizabeth II"), who was also the monarch of other [Commonwealth realms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_realm "Commonwealth realm").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-2) The monarch was represented in Ghana by a governor-general.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-3) Ghana became a [republic within the Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republics_in_the_Commonwealth_of_Nations "Republics in the Commonwealth of Nations") under the Constitution of 1960 and the monarch and governor-general were replaced by an executive president.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-4)[Kwame Nkrumah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwame_Nkrumah "Kwame Nkrumah"), who had been [prime minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_minister_of_Ghana "Prime minister of Ghana") since independence, became the first president, holding office until he was overthrown in a [1966 coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_Ghanaian_coup_d'%C3%A9tat "1966 Ghanaian coup d'état") orchestrated by the American CIA[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-5).

Civilian rule was restored in 1969, with the establishment of the Second Republic. In response to Nkrumah's authoritarian excesses, the constitution drafted a year earlier greatly reduced the powers of the president, to a point almost entirely ceremonial. Real power was vested in the prime minister and cabinet. The only president under this system, [Edward Akufo-Addo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Akufo-Addo "Edward Akufo-Addo"), was elected by parliament in 1970, but was overthrown in a [1972 coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Ghanaian_coup_d'%C3%A9tat "1972 Ghanaian coup d'état").

In 1979, a new constitution established the Third Republic, based on a mixture of the 1960 and 1969 constitutions. The presidency became an executive post once again, with powers and duties similar to those of his American counterpart. The only president under this system, [Hilla Limann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilla_Limann "Hilla Limann"), was elected in 1979, only to be overthrown in a [1981 coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_Ghanaian_coup_d'%C3%A9tat "1981 Ghanaian coup d'état").

In 1992, the current constitution was adopted. Like its 1979 predecessor, it made the presidency an executive post. [Jerry Rawlings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Rawlings "Jerry Rawlings"), the country's de facto leader since the 1981 coup, was elected as president that year, taking office in 1993.

## Eligibility

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=President_of_Ghana&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Eligibility")]

According to Chapter 8, Article 62 of the 1992 Constitution of Ghana, a presidential candidate must meet the following requirements:

*   (a) is a citizen of Ghana by birth
*   (b) has attained the age of forty years; and
*   (c) is a person who is otherwise qualified to be elected a Member of Parliament, except that the disqualifications set out in paragraphs (c), (d), and (e) of clause (2) of article 94 of this [Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution "Constitution") shall not be removed, in respect of any such person, by a presidential pardon or by the lapse of time as provided for in clause (5) of that article.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-The_President_-_Chapter_008-6)

Presidential candidates must lodge a nomination document signed by at least two registered voters in each [district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Districts_of_Ghana "Districts of Ghana"), and includes the name of a [vice presidential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_Ghana "Vice President of Ghana") running mate.

The president serves a four-year term. He is limited to two terms, whether successive or separated. The first president for whom the term limits applied was [Jerry Rawlings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Rawlings "Jerry Rawlings") in 2001.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-termlimits-7)

If the president dies, resigns, is permanently incapacitated, or is removed from office, the vice president automatically ascends as president for the balance of the term. If the vice president ascends to the presidency before more than half of the presidential term expires, the vice president is only allowed to run for a single full term as president. If more than half of the term has expired, the vice president is allowed to run for two full terms. For example, when [John Atta-Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Atta-Mills "John Atta-Mills") died in 2012, Vice President John Mahama served the last six months of Mills' term before being elected in his own right later that year. He was eligible for a second term in 2016, but lost. He lost again in 2020 but won in 2024. However, he will have to leave office for good in 2029. If both the president and vice president are unable to perform the duties of president, the Speaker of Parliament becomes acting president, and new elections must be held within three months.

## Oath of office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=President_of_Ghana&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Oath of office")]

The president of Ghana must be sworn in by the [chief justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Justice_of_Ghana "Chief Justice of Ghana") before Parliament and the [citizens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizenship "Citizenship") of Ghana. The president-elect must repeat the following:

"I, _______________ having been elected to the high office of President of the Republic of Ghana do (in the name of the Almighty God swear) (solemnly affirm) that I will be faithful and true to the Republic of Ghana; that I will at all times preserve, protect and defend the Constitution of the Republic of Ghana; and that I dedicate myself to the service and well-being of the people of the Republic of Ghana and to do right to all manner of persons.

I further (solemnly swear) (solemnly affirm) that should I at any time break this oath of office; I shall submit myself to the laws of the Republic of Ghana and suffer the penalty for it. (So help me God)".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-8)

## Insignia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=President_of_Ghana&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Insignia")]

After the oath of office has been taken by the elected president, these following insignia are handed over to the president. These devices are used to display the rank of his/her office and are used on special occasions.

## Powers and duties of the president

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=President_of_Ghana&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Powers and duties of the president")]

| Presidential styles of **John Dramani Mahama** |
| --- |
| [![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Seal_of_the_Presidency_of_the_Republic_of_Ghana.svg/120px-Seal_of_the_Presidency_of_the_Republic_of_Ghana.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Seal_of_the_Presidency_of_the_Republic_of_Ghana.svg) |
| [Reference style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Style_(manner_of_address) "Style (manner of address)") | 'His Excellency President of the Republic of Ghana" |
| Spoken style | Your Excellency" |
| Alternative style | Mr. President |

Chapter 8 of the Constitution of Ghana states the duties and the powers of the president. The president is required to:

*   uphold the Constitution
*   exercise executive authority
*   preserve the safety and homeland of Ghana.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-The_President_-_Chapter_008-6)

Also, the president is given the powers:

*   as the leader of the [executive branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_branch "Executive branch") of government
*   as the [commander-in-chief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander-in-chief "Commander-in-chief") of the [military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_Ghana "Military of Ghana")
*   to [declare war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_war "Declaration of war")
*   to hold [referendums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referendum "Referendum") regarding issues of national importance
*   to issue [executive orders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decree "Decree")
*   to issue [medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medals "Medals") in honor of service for the nation
*   to issue pardons
*   to declare a [state of emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_emergency "State of emergency") suspending all laws or enacting a state of [martial law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_law "Martial law").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-The_President_-_Chapter_008-6)

The president may execute or cause to be executed treaties, agreements or conventions in the name of the Republic of Ghana.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-The_President_-_Chapter_008-6) The president shall take precedence over the populace of the Republic of Ghana and may refer important policy matters to a national referendum, declare war, conclude peace and other treaties, appoint senior public officials, and grant amnesty (with the concurrence of the [Parliament of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Ghana "Parliament of Ghana")).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-The_President_-_Chapter_008-6) In times of serious internal or external turmoil or threat, or economic or financial crises, the president may assume emergency powers "for the maintenance of national security or public peace and order".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-The_President_-_Chapter_008-6)

The president shall be removed from office if found, in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution, Chapter 8 section 69 (ii) – prejudicial or inimical to the economy or the security of the Republic of Ghana.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-The_President_-_Chapter_008-6) The president shall cease to hold office on the date the [Parliament of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Ghana "Parliament of Ghana") votes to remove the president from office.

## Presidential aircraft

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=President_of_Ghana&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Presidential aircraft")]

The official presidential aircraft is a [Dassault Falcon 900](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dassault_Falcon_900 "Dassault Falcon 900"), registration 9G-EXE, which was acquired in 2010.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-10) The aircraft was overhauled for six months in 2022, and returned to service in February 2023.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-11)

The presidential aircraft uses the colour scheme of the [flag of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_Ghana "Flag of Ghana") in stripes, with the [Ghanaian coat of arms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_Ghana "Coat of arms of Ghana") on the tail.

In 2011, the government purchased an [Embraer 190](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embraer_190 "Embraer 190") making a part payment of $55m however it was revealed in 2020 that the jet was not delivered. There has been some speculation to whether or not the delivery was cancelled due to the government defaulting on its payment.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-12)

## Overview

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=President_of_Ghana&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Overview")]

The youngest person to become head of state was [Jerry Rawlings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Rawlings "Jerry Rawlings"), who at the age of 31, assumed office following [a coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_Ghanaian_coup_d'%C3%A9tat "1979 Ghanaian coup d'état") in 1979.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-13) The youngest civilian head of state to assume the presidency was [Hilla Limann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilla_Limann "Hilla Limann"), who was inaugurated at the age of 44. The oldest person to assume the presidency is [Nana Akufo-Addo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nana_Akufo-Addo "Nana Akufo-Addo") who was inaugurated at age 72.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-15)

At age 34, [Akwasi Afrifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akwasi_Afrifa "Akwasi Afrifa") was the youngest head of state at the end of his tenure. [Fred Akuffo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Akuffo "Fred Akuffo")'s lifespan of 42 years was the shortest of any head of state.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ghana#cite_note-17) The oldest head of state at the end of his tenure is also Nana Akufo-Addo at 80.

Akufo-Addo's second retirement, now 1 year, 271 days, is currently the shortest,  while [Joseph Arthur Ankrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Arthur_Ankrah "Joseph Arthur Ankrah")'s retirement of 23 years is the longest in Ghana's history. At age 87, [John Kufuor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kufuor "John Kufuor") is the oldest of the three living heads of state, he is also the nation's longest-lived head of state. Kufuor and [Nana Akufo-Addo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nana_Akufo-Addo "Nana Akufo-Addo") are the only heads of state to have lived into their 80s. The youngest living head of state is [John Mahama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mahama "John Mahama"), age 67.

The **Bank of Ghana** (**BoG**) is the [Central Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_bank "Central bank") of [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana"). It is located in [Accra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra "Accra") and was formed in 1957.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-Bank_of_Ghana,_Biography-2) The Bank of Ghana has Seven Regional Offices in addition to its head office in Accra. The regional offices are located in the following cities, [Hohoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hohoe "Hohoe"), [Kumasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumasi "Kumasi"), [Sunyani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunyani "Sunyani"), [Tamale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamale,_Ghana "Tamale, Ghana"), [Takoradi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sekondi-Takoradi "Sekondi-Takoradi"), [Bolgatanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolgatanga "Bolgatanga"), Wa. The regional offices are responsible for implementing the policies and directives of the Bank of Ghana in their respective regions. They also provide banking services to the government, financial institutions, and the public.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-3)

The [bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank "Bank") is active in developing [financial inclusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_inclusion "Financial inclusion") policies and is a member of the Alliance for Financial Inclusion.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-:3-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-:0-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-:1-6)

In mid-2026,the central bank expressed strong confidence that [cedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghanaian_cedi "Ghanaian cedi") stability will endure as pressure from the US dollar began easing.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-7)

## Establishment of the Bank of Ghana

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bank_of_Ghana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Establishment of the Bank of Ghana")]

The Bank of Ghana was formally established on 4 March 1957, just two days before [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana")'s declaration of political independence.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-Bank_of_Ghana,_Biography-2)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-8)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-:0-5) The [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire") Parliament passed the Bank of Ghana Ordinance (No. 34) of 1957 to make it official.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-Bank_of_Ghana,_Biography-2) By mid-July 1957, all necessary preparations were completed for the official inauguration of the Bank's new Head Office on High Street.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-:0-5)

Since 1957, the Bank of Ghana has experienced various [legislative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legislature "Legislature") changes.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-Bank_of_Ghana,_Biography-2) The original Bank of Ghana Ordinance (No.34) of 1957 was replaced by the Bank of Ghana Act (1963), Act 182, which was later amended by the Bank of Ghana (Amendment Act) 1965, (Act 282). Eventually, the Bank of Ghana Law, 1992 PNDCL 291, consolidated the legal framework for the bank by repealing both Acts 182 and 282.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-:1-6)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-:0-5)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bank_of_Ghana&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/Ghana_Economy_%E2%80%93_Inflation.jpg/500px-Ghana_Economy_%E2%80%93_Inflation.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ghana_Economy_%E2%80%93_Inflation.jpg)

Ghana economical [inflation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflation "Inflation") rate of change in [percentage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percentage "Percentage")

The Central Bank of Ghana traces its roots to the [Bank of the Gold Coast (BGC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Commercial_Bank "Ghana Commercial Bank") or [Ghana Commercial Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GCB_Bank "GCB Bank"), where it was nurtured. As soon as local politicians and economists saw political [independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence "Independence") in sight in the mid-1950s the agitation for a central bank was revived. It was argued that a central bank was one institution which would give true meaning to political independence. It may be recalled that way back in 1947, some leading politicians had called for the establishment of a national bank, with central bank functions to act as banker to government and to cater for the indigenous sector of the economy.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-10)

Proposals of the advocates for a central bank were accepted and in early 1955, another select committee was set up by the government to take a new look at the Trevor Report and prepare the grounds for the establishment of a central bank in [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana"). The [BGC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Commercial_Bank "Ghana Commercial Bank") had already set the stage for central banking: all that was needed was specially trained personnel in central banking and suitable accommodation for the bank to take off.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-:0-5)

By the end of 1956, all was set for the establishment of the Bank of Ghana. A new and modern five-storey building had been put up on the High Street, adjacent to the [Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra_Metropolitan_Assembly "Accra Metropolitan Assembly") to house both the Bank of Ghana and the [Ghana Commercial Bank (GCB).](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GCB_Bank "GCB Bank")[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-11)

In March 2012, the Bank of Ghana announced it would be making specific commitments to financial inclusion under the [Maya Declaration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Maya_Declaration#Additional_Commitment_Pledges "The Maya Declaration").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-13)

## Governance of the Bank of Ghana

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bank_of_Ghana&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Governance of the Bank of Ghana")]

The first governor of the bank was [Mr. Alfred Eggleston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Eggleston "Alfred Eggleston"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-Bank_of_Ghana,_Biography-2) the former managing director of BGC and an accomplished Scottish banker on secondment to [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") from the [Imperial Bank of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Bank_of_India "Imperial Bank of India"). His deputy [governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor "Governor") was one Mr. Douglas F. Stone, another renowned British central banker also on secondment from [Bank of England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_England "Bank of England").

The general administration of the bank was entrusted in the hands of a seven-member board of directors under the chairmanship of the governor.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-:0-5)

The first board was as follows:

1.   [Alfred Eggleston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Eggleston "Alfred Eggleston"), chairman
2.   Douglas F. Stone, deputy governor
3.   [R. S. Blay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Samuel_Blay "Robert Samuel Blay"), director
4.   N. T. Clerk, director
5.   C. E. Osei, director
6.   R. C. Parkin, director

The [governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor "Governor") of the bank and his deputy were appointed by the governor of the [Gold Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Coast_(British_colony) "Gold Coast (British colony)") on the recommendation of the [prime minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_minister "Prime minister"), in accordance with Section 10 (1) of the 1957 Ordinance. The governor and his deputy were each appointed for a term of five years and were eligible for reappointment. Those two officials were answerable to the board for their acts and decisions in the course of general administration of the affairs of the bank. The board itself was also answerable to the Ministry of Finance for efficient management of the bank. The other directors of the board were also appointed by the Prime Minister with the approval of the governor of the Gold Coast for a term of three years, subject to renewal.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-14)

## Departments

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bank_of_Ghana&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Departments")]

In 1957, the bank commenced business with six main departments namely:[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-19)

*   The governors' office
*   The administration/personnel department
*   The banking department
*   The issue department
*   Accounts/audit department
*   Economics/statistics department

The governors' office was headed by the secretary to the board, while the other departments were headed by managers who reported directly to the deputy governor or in special cases to the governor. The departments were run by the managers in accordance, with policies and decisions arrived at by an in-house [management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Management "Management") accordance with policies arrived at by an in-house management [committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Committee "Committee") comprising the governor, the deputy governor and three or four heads of department appointed by the governor.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-:1-6)

With that initial organisational arrangements, the Bank of Ghana assumed its central role in the banking system of Ghana, which then comprised the central bank, two [expatriate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expatriate "Expatriate") commercial banks – the [British Bank of West Africa (BBWA) (_now Standard Chartered Bank_)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_Chartered "Standard Chartered") and [Barclays Bank Limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays "Barclays") (Dominion, Colonial and Overseas); and the new [Ghana Commercial Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GCB_Bank "GCB Bank") (_GCB_).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-20)

There was also the [Post Office Savings Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/POSB_Bank "POSB Bank") (POSB), which was in fact, not a bank by definition; it was only an institution set up by the [government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government "Government") to mobilize public savings through the agency of the numerous post offices in the country, for investment in government paper.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-21)

Relations with the other banks in the system were set out under sections 39 – 42 of the 1957 Ordinance. Initially, the relation were not very strong. The [Central Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_bank "Central bank") was to act as banker to other banks and co-operate with them to promote and maintain adequate and reasonable banking services for the public. It was also to ensure high standards of conduct and management in the banking system. The bank was also given powers to require the banks to maintain a proportion of their assets in specified form and to submit monthly returns on their operation to the Central Bank. However, banking supervision or bank examination was not specifically highlighted in the Ordinance.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-22)

The bank's FinTech head emphasized in 2026 that mobile money transaction histories should be leveraged to unlock loans and insurance structures for informal sector workers.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-23)

## Functions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bank_of_Ghana&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Functions")]

As a Central Bank of Ghana, it function is as follows:

*   Formulate and implement a monetary policy aimed at achieving the objectives of the Bank;
*   Promote by monetary measure the stabilization of the value of the currency within and outside Ghana;
*   Institute measures that are likely to have a favorable effect on the balance of payments, the state of public finances, and the general development of the national economy;
*   Regulate, supervise, and direct the banking and credit system and ensure the smooth operation of the financial sector;
*   Promote, regulate, and supervise payment and settlement systems;
*   Issue and redeem the currency notes and coins;
*   Ensure effective maintenance and management of Ghana's external financial services;
*   license, regulate, promote, and supervise non-banking financial institutions;
*   Act as banker and financial adviser to the Government;
*   Promote and maintain relations with international banking and financial institutions and subject to the Constitution or any other relevant enactment, implement international monetary agreements to which Ghana is a party; and
*   Do all other things that are incidental or conducive to the efficient performance of its functions under this Act and any other enactment.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-:0-5)
*   In 2026,the bank reported a 40% drop in internal staff [fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud") though cash theft remained a persistent industry issue.

In August 2019, Dr. Papa Kwesi Nduom and other individuals filed a lawsuit against the Bank of Ghana and other parties concerning the cancellation of the license of GN Bank/Savings.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-24)

#### _New Bank of Ghana Headquarters_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bank_of_Ghana&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: New Bank of Ghana Headquarters")]

In August 2023, the Bank of [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") through a press briefing described with justifications, its move to building a [new headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bank_Square "The Bank Square") to replace its current building. The Bank of Ghana in Accra released a document on August 21, 2023, containing this disclosure.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-:2-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-31)

The decision to build the new edifice was met with mixed reactions as the Minority in Parliament of Ghana and some Civil Society Organizations strongly opposed the new building, stating that such projects are unnecessary given the current economic situation of the country.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-:2-26) Consequently, they criticized the Governor of the Bank of Ghana and his deputies, urging them to step down and declared their plan to stage a protest at the Bank of Ghana on September 5, 2023, seeking the departure of these officials.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-:2-26)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-32)

Other distinguished members of the society including the Dormaahene, Osagyefo Oseadeeyo Agyemang Badu II have also expressed their reservations towards the decision of the Bank of Ghana's leadership.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-35)

On the other side, the Deputy Minister for Trade, Dr Stephen Amoah, called the action of those calling for the resignation of the governor as unnecessary.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana#cite_note-36)

**Mahamudu Bawumia** (born 7 October 1963) is a [Ghanaian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") politician and former central banker who served as the seventh [vice president of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_Ghana "Vice President of Ghana") from 7 January 2017 to 7 January 2025 under President [Nana Akufo-Addo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nana_Akufo-Addo "Nana Akufo-Addo").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-10) He was the [New Patriotic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Patriotic_Party "New Patriotic Party") (NPP) nominee for president in the [2024 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Ghanaian_general_election "2024 Ghanaian general election").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-11)

He also ran as the NPP vice-presidential candidate in the 2012 general elections and was the lead witness for the petitioners in the 2012/2013 Presidential Election Petition, which challenged the declaration of [John Mahama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mahama "John Mahama") as winner of the election.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-15) He holds a PhD in Economics from [Simon Fraser University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Fraser_University "Simon Fraser University").

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mahamudu_Bawumia&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

A member of [Mamprusi people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mamprusi_people "Mamprusi people"), Bawumia was born in [Tamale Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamale,_Ghana "Tamale, Ghana"), to Alhaji [Mumuni Bawumia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumuni_Bawumia "Mumuni Bawumia") and Hajia Mariama Bawumia. He is the twelfth of his father's 18 children and the second of his mother's five children.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-18)

Mahamudu Bawumia attended the [Sakasaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakasaka "Sakasaka") primary school in Tamale[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-19) and gained admission to [Tamale Secondary School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamale_Senior_High_School "Tamale Senior High School") in 1975. After graduating from Tamale Secondary School, he went to the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), where he studied banking and obtained the Chartered Institute of Bankers Diploma (ACIB). He was the president of the Ghana United Nations Students' Association (GUNSA) in 1981. He took a First Class Honours Degree in Economics at [Buckingham University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Buckingham "University of Buckingham") in 1987.

He then obtained a master's degree in economics at [Lincoln College, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_College,_Oxford "Lincoln College, Oxford"), and obtained a PhD in economics at the [Simon Fraser University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Fraser_University "Simon Fraser University"), [Vancouver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver "Vancouver"), British Columbia, Canada in 1995.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-sfu-20) His areas of specialization include [macroeconomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macroeconomics "Macroeconomics"), [international economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_economics "International economics"), [development economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Development_economics "Development economics") and [monetary policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monetary_policy "Monetary policy"). He has numerous publications.

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mahamudu_Bawumia&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

From 1988 to 1990, Bawumia worked as a lecturer in monetary economics and international finance at the [Emile Woolf College](https://www.emilewoolf.com/) of Accountancy in London; England. He also served as an intern at the Research Department of the [International Monetary Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund "International Monetary Fund") in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") Bawumia also served as resident representative of the [African Development Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Development_Bank "African Development Bank") in [Zimbabwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe "Zimbabwe").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-21)

Between 1996 and 2000, Bawumia served as an assistant professor of economics in the Hankamer School of Business at [Baylor University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baylor_University "Baylor University") in [Waco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waco "Waco"), [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas"), and USA, where he received a Young Researcher Award in 1998. He was listed in "Who Is Who Among America's Teachers” in 1999. He also published two books on monetary policy and economic development.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-22)

Bawumia returned to Ghana in 2000 to work as an economist at the [Bank of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana "Bank of Ghana"). He rose from Senior Economist to Head of Department and subsequently served as Special Assistant to the governor of the bank. President [John Kufuor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kufuor "John Kufuor") appointed Bawumia as [deputy governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_governor "Deputy governor") of the Bank of Ghana in June 2006.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-23)

At the Bank of Ghana, Mahamudu Bawumia

*   Served as head of the Monetary Policy and Financial Stability Department, he was part of the team that designed and implemented the inflation-targeting framework that continues to guide monetary policy and the workings of the Monetary Policy Committee at the Bank of Ghana. The inflation-targeting framework established reduced inflation from over 40% in 2000 to 10.2% by 2007 (i.e., before the oil price shock of 2007/2008) while maintaining relative exchange rate stability.
*   Was part of the team that was instrumental in designing and implementing policy initiatives, such as the abolition of the secondary reserve requirements and the opening up of the banking sector to competition. This resulted in a major increase in the availability of credit to the private sector from 12.5% of [GDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_domestic_product "Gross domestic product") in 2001 to 28.5% of GDP by 2008.
*   Led the Bank of Ghana's technical negotiation team and was on the government team that negotiated with the World Bank and International Monetary Fund since 2001 through [HIPC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavily_indebted_poor_countries "Heavily indebted poor countries") and [PRGF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_Reduction_and_Growth_Facility "Poverty Reduction and Growth Facility"). Partly as a result of these negotiations, Ghana by 2007 successfully ended its dependence on [IMF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund "International Monetary Fund") assistance.
*   Served as a member of the government technical negotiating team on HIPC Paris Club and Completion Point Negotiations. Ghana completed the HIPC process successfully with significant debt relief of close to $4 billion.
*   Was a member of the Government Team to Negotiate the [Millennium Challenge Account Compact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_Challenge_Corporation "Millennium Challenge Corporation") with the US government. The MCA resulted in many significant projects, such as the George Bush Highway.
*   Was a member of the Government Technical Team on the Deregulation of Ghana's Petroleum Sector.
*   As chairman of the Capital Markets Committee, was responsible for the strategy for accessing the international capital markets with a debut [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US$ "US$")750 million, which was four times oversubscribed.
*   Was part of the team that designed and implemented the successful redenomination of the cedi. Through this process, the cedi was considerably strengthened. Significant savings were also made by the Bank of Ghana in currency printing costs.
*   Was involved in the design and implementation of the e-zwich common platform for all banks, savings and loans companies and rural banks, offering interoperability across different financial institutions.
*   As the deputy governor in charge of financial stability, oversaw the soundness of the banking sector.
*   As deputy governor, Bawumia served on the Boards of the Bank of Ghana, Ghana International Bank (UK), [Ghana Telecom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Telecom "Ghana Telecom"), Revenue Agencies Governing Board, [Social Security and National Insurance Trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Security_and_National_Insurance_Trust "Social Security and National Insurance Trust").

Shortly before the 2008 election, Bawumia resigned as deputy governor at the [Bank of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Ghana "Bank of Ghana").

### 2008 elections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mahamudu_Bawumia&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2008 elections")]

Mahamudu Bawumia was running mate to the New Patriotic Party candidate in the 2008 elections, Nana Akufo-Addo.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-26) The NPP increased its share of the vote compared to 2004 in all the three Northern Regions, in both the first and second round.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-:0-27)

### 2008–2011

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mahamudu_Bawumia&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2008–2011")]

Bawumia served as a consultant to the Economic Commission of Africa between February and March 2009. Between April and October 2009, he was a visiting scholar at the [University of British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_British_Columbia "University of British Columbia")[Liu Centre for Global Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Institute_for_Global_Issues "Liu Institute for Global Issues") and [UBC Fisheries Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UBC_Fisheries_Centre "UBC Fisheries Centre").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-:0-27)

In October 2009, he was appointed as a Fellow of the [International Growth Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Growth_Centre "International Growth Centre") (IGC), a research institute based jointly at the London School of Economics and Political Science and [Oxford University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford") that provides advice on economic growth to governments of developing countries, specifically serving as an IGC Team Member for [Sierra Leone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Leone "Sierra Leone"). He also served as an advisor to the Central Bank of Sierra Leone on the redesigning of the organizational structure of the bank and its monetary policy framework.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-:1-28)

Between October 2009 and October 2010, he was a senior research associate at the Centre for the Study of African Economies at the Department of Economics, University of Oxford. In January 2011, Bawumia was appointed resident representative of the [African Development Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Development_Bank "African Development Bank") for [Zimbabwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe "Zimbabwe") by the African Development Bank. He served in this position until reappointed as the vice-presidential candidate to Nana Akufo-Addo on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party for Ghana's 2012 presidential election.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-:1-28)

### 2012 elections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mahamudu_Bawumia&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2012 elections")]

Bawumia was re-nominated as the Vice-Presidential Candidate to [Nana Akufo-Addo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nana_Akufo-Addo "Nana Akufo-Addo") for the 2012 General Elections in March 2012.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-29)

The party won 10 seats in the [Northern Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Region_(Ghana) "Northern Region (Ghana)") including Yendi, Walewale, Yagaba – Kubore, Bunkpurugu, Bimbilla, Chereponi, Kpandai, Tatale – Sanguli, Tolon and Zabzugu. It also won the Nabdam and Talensi Constituencies in the [Upper East Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_East_Region "Upper East Region"). Overall, Nana Akufo-Addo and Bawumia lost the presidential elections to [John Dramani Mahama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mahama "John Mahama").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### 2016 elections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mahamudu_Bawumia&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2016 elections")]

[Nana Akuffo-Addo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nana_Akuffo-Addo "Nana Akuffo-Addo") appointed Bawumia as his running mate in the 2016 presidential election.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-31)

### 2024 elections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mahamudu_Bawumia&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2024 elections")]

On Friday, 16 June 2023, Bawumia filed his nomination to contest in the NPP Presidential primaries.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-32) As part of the presidential primaries, Bawumia picked the tenth position after balloting for the selection of five contest for the final selection of the presidential candidate for the NPP in the 2024 election.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-33) Bawumia, on 26 August 2023, won the super delegates congress election by the [New Patriotic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Patriotic_Party "New Patriotic Party") with 68%, beating nine other candidates in the build up to the party’s national delegates congress to elect their flagbearer.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-34)

Bawumia has been elected to lead the New Patriotic Party (NPP) for Election 2024 as flagbearer. Bawumia won NPP presidential primary with 61.43% of total valid votes cast which happened on 4 November 2023 at 276 constituencies across the country and the Party Headquarters, Asylum Down, Accra.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-37)

On Tuesday, 9 July 2024, Bawumia unveiled Dr. [Matthew Opoku Prempeh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Opoku_Prempeh "Matthew Opoku Prempeh") as his running mate for the 2024 general elections.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-41) The unveiling took place at Jubilee Park in [Kumasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumasi "Kumasi").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-43)

On 8 December 2024, Bawumia conceded defeat to former President [John Mahama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mahama "John Mahama") in an address to the media at his residence.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-45)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mahamudu_Bawumia&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Bawumia is married to [Samira Bawumia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samira_Bawumia "Samira Bawumia") and they have four children.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-46) He is a member of the [Mabia (Mossi-Dagbon)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gur_languages "Gur languages") ethnicity, shares same heritage with influential figures as [Thomas Sankara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Sankara "Thomas Sankara"), [Alhassane Ouattara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alassane_Ouattara "Alassane Ouattara"), [Haruna Iddrisu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haruna_Iddrisu "Haruna Iddrisu"), among others.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-47) He is a [Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim "Muslim").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-48) Bawumia was named after [Yaa Naa Mahamadu Bila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_kings_of_Dagbon "List of kings of Dagbon"), a [king](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yaa_Naa "Yaa Naa") of [Dagbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Dagbon "Kingdom of Dagbon") who ruled from 1948 to 1953.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-49) The name Bawumia means "They have heard" in [Dagbanli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dagbani_language "Dagbani language") and [Gmampruli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mampruli_language "Mampruli language") languages. An avid sports fan, he is a supporter of English club [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-50)

## Philanthropy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mahamudu_Bawumia&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Philanthropy")]

The Vice President is known for several philanthropic works. In October 2020, he formally commissioned an ultramodern mosque built and fully funded by him for use by the people of Prang in the Bono East area.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-51) Dr. Bawumia had earlier in June same year settle over nearly 6 decades land lease arrears for the [Kumasi Central Mosque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumasi_Central_Mosque "Kumasi Central Mosque").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-52)

In September 2021, Bawumia pledged GHS 1,500 monthly stipend to [Psalm Adjeteyfio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psalm_Adjeteyfio "Psalm Adjeteyfio") to take care of his rent and upkeep.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-53) In May 2022, Dr. Bawumia donated an amount of GHs 20,000.00 to a taxi driver who returned missing GHs 8,400.00 to the owner.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-54) In October 2021, Dr. Bawumia celebrated his 58th birthday with inmates of the Weija Leprosarium.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-55) In October 2022, he celebrated his birthday with cured lepers from the Weija Leprosarium[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-56) and in October 2023, he celebrated his 60th birthday with the orphans at the Kumasi Children's Home.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamudu_Bawumia#cite_note-57)

As an entrepreneur, it’s no surprise that Monopoly is one of my favorite board games. In fact, I’d go so far as to say I’m one of the best players out there (humble brag)! 😉 This classic game isn’t just about rolling dice and moving pieces—it’s a thrilling simulation of life, business, and strategy. It’s about domineering the board, crushing your opponents, and ultimately becoming the richest player. But beyond the competition, Monopoly teaches essential real-life skills: 💡 Financial Literacy – From budgeting to investing in assets that pay off in the long run. 💡 Negotiation – Striking the right deal at the right time. 💡 Risk Management – Knowing when to take chances and when to play it safe. 💡 Perseverance – Even when you’re sent to jail or hit with unexpected fees! Dammnnn those Taxes always hit differently!! Monopoly reflects the entrepreneurial spirit—the drive to succeed, the thrill of competition, and the satisfaction of building something lasting. Every time I play, I feel my innate desire to strategize, dominate, and grow wealth being tested and sharpened. # Sunderland University graduate Joojo Kyei-Sarpong hoping to develop rehab board game Inspirado to help with substance misuse

13th October 2017

[Tyne And Wear](link_67)

[![Image 2: Tony Kearney Profile Image](link_68)](https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/author/profile/2289.Tony_Kearney/ [link_69])

[By Tony Kearney](link_69)News Editor (North Durham)

![Image 4: INSPIRATIONAL: Sunderland graduate Joojo Kyei-Sarpong has developed the board game to help people recovering from substance misuse](https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/resources/images/6937496.jpg?type=mds-article-575%20575w)

INSPIRATIONAL: Sunderland graduate Joojo Kyei-Sarpong has developed the board game to help people recovering from substance misuse

![Image 5: USA Today logo](https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/resources/responsive-static/images/usa-today-logo.svg)

 This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. 

A BOARD game has been created by a university graduate to help people recover from substance misuse.

Inspirado is designed to be used in group therapy and rehab sessions.

Players begin as a caterpillar, hoping to finish as a butterfly, passing series of alert tiles on the way where they play through behaviour cards and inspirational cards.

[](link_72)

The game was developed by Sunderland University graduate Joojo Kyei-Sarpong, who dedicated his career to supporting those living with addiction, after losing a friend through a drug overdose.

The 35-year-old has now launched a crowdfunding campaign to raise £5,000 for the game to be manufactured.

He said: “My approach to coaching has always been illustrative and compassionate, using everyday examples to help clients understand behaviour change.

“This motivated me to create the game as an intervention, with the potential to be a resource for substance misuse treatment”.

# Sunderland University graduate Joojo Kyei-Sarpong hoping to develop rehab board game Inspirado to help with substance misuse

13th October 2017

[Tyne And Wear](link_67)

[![Image 2: Tony Kearney Profile Image](link_68)](https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/author/profile/2289.Tony_Kearney/ [link_69])

[By Tony Kearney](link_69)News Editor (North Durham)

[![Image 3: comment icon](https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/resources/responsive-static/mds/images/icons/message.svg)0 comments](https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/comments/15592939/ [link_70])

![Image 4: INSPIRATIONAL: Sunderland graduate Joojo Kyei-Sarpong has developed the board game to help people recovering from substance misuse](https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/resources/images/6937496.jpg?type=mds-article-575%20575w)

INSPIRATIONAL: Sunderland graduate Joojo Kyei-Sarpong has developed the board game to help people recovering from substance misuse

![Image 5: USA Today logo](https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/resources/responsive-static/images/usa-today-logo.svg)

 This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. 

A BOARD game has been created by a university graduate to help people recover from substance misuse.

Inspirado is designed to be used in group therapy and rehab sessions.

Players begin as a caterpillar, hoping to finish as a butterfly, passing series of alert tiles on the way where they play through behaviour cards and inspirational cards.

[](link_72)

The game was developed by Sunderland University graduate Joojo Kyei-Sarpong, who dedicated his career to supporting those living with addiction, after losing a friend through a drug overdose.

The 35-year-old has now launched a crowdfunding campaign to raise £5,000 for the game to be manufactured.

He said: “My approach to coaching has always been illustrative and compassionate, using everyday examples to help clients understand behaviour change.

“This motivated me to create the game as an intervention, with the potential to be a resource for substance misuse treatment”.

Meta Pay

Meta Pay is an easy, secure way to pay on the apps you already use.

Not in the US? [Check availability](https://l.facebook.com/meta-pay/availability/)

![Image 3: Easy Checkout](https://lookaside.fbsbx.com/elementpath/media/?media_id=3486918374891602&version=1741847833)

![Image 4: Easy Checkout](https://scontent-sea5-1.xx.fbcdn.net/v/t39.8562-6/495359896_2507365742958129_93829394151731422_n.png?_nc_cat=109&ccb=1-7&_nc_sid=f537c7&_nc_ohc=ytYOWpglwAMQ7kNvwFVkv1r&_nc_oc=AdojoPQ3GQ0g9SgtwH9yRCU0KltMAdVjcaRHRsgYWSWOVzYpyZFwD61qn3uY3La0AUjT86FWkI8DCXzbvqRPVum4&_nc_zt=14&_nc_ht=scontent-sea5-1.xx&_nc_gid=-qD9zxSoj-4uRhQjV8KnPQ&_nc_ss=7b289&oh=00_AQPXAnMSayFujRsfxkwcx2W6Asg3UjUiRLpq5L7HDrwbGg&oe=6AC9A5E4)

Shop, donate or send money on the apps you already use

When you use Meta Pay, it loads your saved payment, shipping, and contact information automatically so you can check out quickly.

![Image 5: Check out easily](https://lookaside.fbsbx.com/elementpath/media/?media_id=2095010837510412&version=1741858205)

## Check out easily and quickly

Use Meta Pay when shopping online. If you have Meta Pay set up, your saved payment, shipping, and contact information loads automatically after a quick Facebook or Instagram login verification.

New to Meta Pay? [Add your payment method](https://www.facebook.com/help/503055570507753) once and you'll enjoy a fast checkout every time you use Meta Pay.

![Image 6: Payment management](https://lookaside.fbsbx.com/elementpath/media/?media_id=363669089633515&version=1743144654)

## Manage your payment activity

You can easily manage payment methods, view your payment and transaction history, or access customer support in [Accounts Center](https://www.facebook.com/help/943858526073065).

Your security and protection matter

![Image 7: Anti fraud monitoring](https://lookaside.fbsbx.com/elementpath/media/?media_id=244195221960097&version=1743144654)

![Image 8: Customer support](https://lookaside.fbsbx.com/elementpath/media/?media_id=748828830473261&version=1743144654)

![Image 9: Data security](https://lookaside.fbsbx.com/elementpath/media/?media_id=216003424836249&version=1743144654)

### Anti-fraud monitoring

To detect unauthorized activity, payments are monitored using anti-fraud technology.

[Learn more](https://www.facebook.com/help/2167164950254129)

### Customer support

If an unauthorized Meta Pay transaction appears on your bank account, customer support is always ready to help. Chat live 24 hours a day or reach out via email.

[Learn more](https://www.facebook.com/help/218846068134280)

### Data security

To keep your information secure, your debit and credit card numbers are encrypted for safe and secure storage.

[Learn more](https://www.facebook.com/help/663265547498941)

How it works

It’s simple to get started with Meta Pay

![Image 10: Open the app](https://scontent-sea5-1.xx.fbcdn.net/v/t39.8562-6/513872237_775467235144345_8624751955344441868_n.jpg?_nc_cat=103&ccb=1-7&_nc_sid=f537c7&_nc_ohc=FVDQtYqJjJ0Q7kNvwHCBUXD&_nc_oc=AdqeZ8sLlgOgmCRN_ZTQMEOMQXSqeNEpxjV75DqAxx5Wcbgo93X7ECJ8X9oQfveeQCBMMO5Oe8oUkBevSG0dezkO&_nc_zt=14&_nc_ht=scontent-sea5-1.xx&_nc_gid=-qD9zxSoj-4uRhQjV8KnPQ&_nc_ss=7b289&oh=00_AQNxVLSxEyGB9JHEa3JUu9J-q6_SGf-0EbFboIXGaPXTUA&oe=6AC9989A)

![Image 11: Payment details](https://scontent-sea5-1.xx.fbcdn.net/v/t39.8562-6/511136492_2465734010467893_2761245462987030009_n.jpg?_nc_cat=101&ccb=1-7&_nc_sid=f537c7&_nc_ohc=sLSlhG-YBxAQ7kNvwHsI1QW&_nc_oc=AdpkOGbAfM9oZnk4g_jfozURDXJ4rdHoS-2f-kCxsfd8eCULRz0wc4OppH-FuUMXxGVDNqizj3v0NPn0T1bf5zDt&_nc_zt=14&_nc_ht=scontent-sea5-1.xx&_nc_gid=-qD9zxSoj-4uRhQjV8KnPQ&_nc_ss=7b289&oh=00_AQPJPBEFNtniJs0cFHHoeEMgGd7KzUH1NASGjntqOif1fA&oe=6AC9AF7F)

### Open your favorite app

Start a payment on the apps, such as Facebook, Messenger and Instagram, you already use. There's no need to download a separate app.

### Enter your payment details

Add the credit card, debit card or PayPal account you’d like to use. You can update your preferred payment method any time within Meta Pay settings.

### Create a PIN for Meta Pay

Protect yourself from unauthorized transactions with a personalized PIN to control access. Once it’s enabled, you will be prompted to enter it before some purchases for additional security.

### Manage your payment information

Manage and update your preferred payment method in Accounts Center at any time. You can also view your transaction history across all connected apps in the same Accounts Center.

### Send money

When you're sending money to friends and family, the money goes straight into the recipient’s bank account. There’s no waiting and no fees.

(There may be fees imposed by your bank which are separate from Meta Pay.)

![Image 15: Facebook logo](https://lookaside.fbsbx.com/elementpath/media/?media_id=929256521689681&version=1743144654)![Image 16: Instagram logo](https://lookaside.fbsbx.com/elementpath/media/?media_id=773855684386267&version=1743144654)

## Use Meta Pay seamlessly between Facebook and Instagram

Set up Meta Pay on Facebook by adding your preferred payment just once, then connect it across Instagram without having to re-enter your information each time.

## FAQs

We’ve included some frequently asked questions below. For more, visit [Meta Pay Help Center](https://pay.facebook.com/faqs/#General).

How does Meta Pay work?

Meta Pay is a seamless and secure way to make payments on Facebook, Messenger, Instagram, and in participating online stores. Enter your payment card or account information just once and then use Meta Pay to make purchases, send money or donate. Add a PIN or use the fingerprint or face ID on your device to secure individual payments. Meta Pay also lets you view your payment history, manage payment information and access 24-hour chat service for customer support.

Is it secure to make payments with Meta Pay?

We use advanced technology to keep payment information secure. Meta Pay is protected with:

*   Anti-fraud technology that monitors purchases on Meta Pay systems to detect unauthorized activity.
*   Payment card numbers are securely stored, encrypted and stored separately from your profile data.
*   Notifications that alert you if Meta Pay detects unusual activity.
*   An option to create a PIN or use the fingerprint or face ID on your device for additional security when sending money or making a payment. Facebook does not receive or store your device’s biometric information.

How do I set up a Meta Pay PIN?

When making a payment with Meta Pay, you may be required to set up a PIN (PIN is mandatory in some use cases) by selecting a 4-digit numeric pass code. You may also be able to use your device's face ID or fingerprint for an extra layer of security.

You can also set up a PIN with Meta Pay for additional security when sending payments by going to Orders and Payments settings. As part of our commitment to security, we may prompt a PIN with Meta Pay verification when certain types of transactions appear as unusual activity.

Do I need to have a Facebook account to use Meta Pay?

Meta Pay can be set up by logging into at least one of our apps - Facebook, Instagram or Messenger. Then, enter your payment card or account information. When Meta Pay is set up on Facebook and Messenger, people can connect Meta Pay across Instagram without having to re-enter their payment information.

Where can I use Meta Pay?

Meta Pay can be used on Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, and in participating online stores.

*   On **Facebook**, you can use Meta Pay to shop, donate, buy tickets for events, or games.
*   On **Instagram**, you can use Meta Pay to shop or make donations to charitable or personal fundraisers.
*   On **Messenger**, you can use Meta Pay to send money to friends and family in the United States.
*   When online stores have Meta Pay enabled, you can shop the products and services you love, and check out faster with your saved credentials.

Meta Pay may not be available in all payment use cases on Facebook, Instagram and Messenger. We are continuing to build out functionality so that more people in more places can use Meta Pay across our technologies. Check back here for updates.

As an entrepreneur, it’s no surprise that Monopoly is one of my favorite board games. In fact, I’d go so far as to say I’m one of the best players out there (humble brag)! 😉 This classic game isn’t just about rolling dice and moving pieces—it’s a thrilling simulation of life, business, and strategy. It’s about domineering the board, crushing your opponents, and ultimately becoming the richest player. But beyond the competition, Monopoly teaches essential real-life skills: 💡 Financial Literacy – From budgeting to investing in assets that pay off in the long run. 💡 Negotiation – Striking the right deal at the right time. 💡 Risk Management – Knowing when to take chances and when to play it safe. 💡 Perseverance – Even when you’re sent to jail or hit with unexpected fees! Dammnnn those Taxes always hit differently!! Monopoly reflects the entrepreneurial spirit—the drive to succeed, the thrill of competition, and the satisfaction of building something lasting. Every time I play, I feel my innate desire to strategize, dominate, and grow wealth being tested and sharpened. That’s why I’m throwing out a challenge this holiday season: If you’re in Accra and love Monopoly as much as I do, let’s meet up for a friendly (but competitive!) game. Who knows? We might learn a thing or two from each other—and maybe even spark some collaboration along the way. So, Monopoly fans, let’s connect! Let’s play, strategize, and celebrate the art of winning—both on the board and in life. INSPIRATIONAL: Sunderland graduate Joojo Kyei-Sarpong has developed the board game to help people recovering from substance misuse

![Image 5: USA Today logo](https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/resources/responsive-static/images/usa-today-logo.svg)

 This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. 

A BOARD game has been created by a university graduate to help people recover from substance misuse.

Inspirado is designed to be used in group therapy and rehab sessions.

Players begin as a caterpillar, hoping to finish as a butterfly, passing series of alert tiles on the way where they play through behaviour cards and inspirational cards.

[](https://www.outbrain.com/what-is/default/en)

The game was developed by Sunderland University graduate Joojo Kyei-Sarpong, who dedicated his career to supporting those living with addiction, after losing a friend through a drug overdose.

The 35-year-old has now launched a crowdfunding campaign to raise £5,000 for the game to be manufactured.

He said: “My approach to coaching has always been illustrative and compassionate, using everyday examples to help clients understand behaviour change.

“This motivated me to create the game as an intervention, with the potential to be a resource for substance misuse treatment”.

Shop, donate or send money on the apps you already use

When you use Meta Pay, it loads your saved payment, shipping, and contact information automatically so you can check out quickly.

![Image 5: Check out easily](link_13)

## Check out easily and quickly

Use Meta Pay when shopping online. If you have Meta Pay set up, your saved payment, shipping, and contact information loads automatically after a quick Facebook or Instagram login verification.

New to Meta Pay? [Add your payment method](link_14) once and you'll enjoy a fast checkout every time you use Meta Pay.

![Image 6: Payment management](link_15)

## Manage your payment activity

You can easily manage payment methods, view your payment and transaction history, or access customer support in [Accounts Center](link_16).

Your security and protection matter

![Image 7: Anti fraud monitoring](link_17)

![Image 8: Customer support](link_18)

![Image 9: Data security](link_19)

### Anti-fraud monitoring

To detect unauthorized activity, payments are monitored using anti-fraud technology.

[Learn more](link_20)

### Customer support

If an unauthorized Meta Pay transaction appears on your bank account, customer support is always ready to help. Chat live 24 hours a day or reach out via email.

[Learn more](link_21)

### Data security

To keep your information secure, your debit and credit card numbers are encrypted for safe and secure storage.

[Learn more](link_22)

How it works

It’s simple to get started with Meta Pay

### Open your favorite app

Start a payment on the apps, such as Facebook, Messenger and Instagram, you already use. There's no need to download a separate app.

### Enter your payment details

Add the credit card, debit card or PayPal account you’d like to use. You can update your preferred payment method any time within Meta Pay settings.

### Create a PIN for Meta Pay

Protect yourself from unauthorized transactions with a personalized PIN to control access. Once it’s enabled, you will be prompted to enter it before some purchases for additional security.

### Manage your payment information

Manage and update your preferred payment method in Accounts Center at any time. You can also view your transaction history across all connected apps in the same Accounts Center.

### Send money

When you're sending money to friends and family, the money goes straight into the recipient’s bank account. There’s no waiting and no fees.

(There may be fees imposed by your bank which are separate from Meta Pay.)

![Image 15: Facebook logo](link_23)![Image 16: Instagram logo](link_24)

## Use Meta Pay seamlessly between Facebook and Instagram

Set up Meta Pay on Facebook by adding your preferred payment just once, then connect it across Instagram without having to re-enter your information each time.

## FAQs

We’ve included some frequently asked questions below. For more, visit [Meta Pay Help Center](link_25).

How does Meta Pay work?

Meta Pay is a seamless and secure way to make payments on Facebook, Messenger, Instagram, and in participating online stores. Enter your payment card or account information just once and then use Meta Pay to make purchases, send money or donate. Add a PIN or use the fingerprint or face ID on your device to secure individual payments. Meta Pay also lets you view your payment history, manage payment information and access 24-hour chat service for customer support.

Is it secure to make payments with Meta Pay?

We use advanced technology to keep payment information secure. Meta Pay is protected with:

*   Anti-fraud technology that monitors purchases on Meta Pay systems to detect unauthorized activity.
*   Payment card numbers are securely stored, encrypted and stored separately from your profile data.
*   Notifications that alert you if Meta Pay detects unusual activity.
*   An option to create a PIN or use the fingerprint or face ID on your device for additional security when sending money or making a payment. Facebook does not receive or store your device’s biometric information.

How do I set up a Meta Pay PIN?

When making a payment with Meta Pay, you may be required to set up a PIN (PIN is mandatory in some use cases) by selecting a 4-digit numeric pass code. You may also be able to use your device's face ID or fingerprint for an extra layer of security.

You can also set up a PIN with Meta Pay for additional security when sending payments by going to Orders and Payments settings. As part of our commitment to security, we may prompt a PIN with Meta Pay verification when certain types of transactions appear as unusual activity.

Do I need to have a Facebook account to use Meta Pay?

Meta Pay can be set up by logging into at least one of our apps - Facebook, Instagram or Messenger. Then, enter your payment card or account information. When Meta Pay is set up on Facebook and Messenger, people can connect Meta Pay across Instagram without having to re-enter their payment information.

Where can I use Meta Pay?

Meta Pay can be used on Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, and in participating online stores.

*   On **Facebook**, you can use Meta Pay to shop, donate, buy tickets for events, or games.
*   On **Instagram**, you can use Meta Pay to shop or make donations to charitable or personal fundraisers.
*   On **Messenger**, you can use Meta Pay to send money to friends and family in the United States.
*   When online stores have Meta Pay enabled, you can shop the products and services you love, and check out faster with your saved credentials.

Meta Pay may not be available in all payment use cases on Facebook, Instagram and Messenger. We are continuing to build out functionality so that more people in more places can use Meta Pay across our technologies. Check back here for updates.
